rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Commercial Banks - China Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Published monthly by ChinaBond (China Central Depository & Clearing Co., Ltd.), this series measures the face-value stock of Chinese Government Bonds (CGBs) held by commercial banks on deposit at the central clearing system. Commercial banks are the dominant holders of CGBs, typically accounting for 60–70% of total outstanding, driven by reserve requirements, LCR buffers, and the banks' need for high-quality liquid assets. Releases occur roughly 10–15 business days after month-end.
rics.how_to_use: Track month-on-month changes to gauge whether banks are accumulating or reducing CGB exposure — net buying signals precautionary demand for safe assets or PBOC window guidance; net selling often precedes rate volatility. Combine with aCNHSTCGNA (total CGB holdings) to derive the commercial-bank share and monitor concentration risk. A rising share alongside falling CGB yields (as in 2023–24) can reinforce the 'asset famine' narrative, where banks chase yield into government paper.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Commercial Banks - Credit Asset Backed Securities
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Commercial Banks / ABS
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond data tracking the stock of Credit Asset-Backed Securities (credit ABS) held by commercial banks. Credit ABS in China are primarily auto-loan ABS, corporate-loan CLOs, and credit-card ABS registered via the PBOC-supervised interbank securitisation programme; volumes have grown steadily to over CNY 3 trillion outstanding. Commercial banks invest in senior tranches for capital-efficient yield pickup above NCDs.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a proxy for bank appetite for structured credit. Rising commercial-bank ABS holdings alongside declining NCD rates indicate banks are extending duration and moving down the credit ladder in search of yield. Cross with aCNHCABTOA (total ABS holdings by all investors) to assess the bank share; if banks dominate senior tranches the credit cycle is benign, while a drop in bank holdings can signal concerns about underlying collateral quality.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Credit Cooperatives - Enterprise Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Credit Cooperatives / Enterprise Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond series showing enterprise bonds (企业债) held by rural credit cooperatives and urban credit cooperatives. Enterprise bonds are NDRC-approved bonds issued by state-linked corporates, historically used to fund infrastructure; outstanding has declined as issuers shifted to MTNs and corporate bonds, but legacy stock remains significant. Credit cooperatives are smaller regional lenders with concentrated local exposure.
rics.how_to_use: This niche series is most useful for assessing concentration risk in China's smaller financial institutions. A sustained increase suggests credit cooperatives are compressing yield spreads on enterprise bonds, often a late-cycle signal. Analysts monitoring the resolution of local government financing vehicle (LGFV) debt should watch this alongside aCNBDETBNA to detect shifts in enterprise-bond stock relative to the overall depository base.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Foreign Investors - China Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Foreign Investors / CGBs
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond statistic tracking the face-value stock of Chinese Government Bonds held by offshore (foreign) investors via Bond Connect, CIBM Direct, and QFII/RQFII channels. Foreign holdings of CGBs peaked above CNY 2.6 trillion (~USD 360 billion) in late 2021 after CGB inclusion in the FTSE WGBI and Bloomberg Global Aggregate indices, then fell to around CNY 1.7 trillion by 2023–24 amid a widening CGB-UST yield gap. Published roughly 10–15 days after each month-end.
rics.how_to_use: The single most watched foreign-flow variable in China's bond market. A sustained decline in foreign CGB holdings signals capital outflow pressure on the CNY and may presage PBoC FX intervention; a reversal typically coincides with CGB yield stabilisation or CNY appreciation expectations. Pair with aCNXRUSD (USD/CNY) and aCNHSFIPNA (foreign holdings of policy bank bonds) to construct a total foreign bond-flow picture. Month-on-month changes proxy net portfolio investment in balance-of-payments analysis.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Foreign Investors - Commercial Bank Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Foreign Investors / Commercial Bank Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond data on foreign investors' holdings of Chinese commercial bank bonds (financial bonds, Tier-2 capital bonds, and NCDs issued by banks). Foreign appetite for bank bonds is driven by yield pickup over CGBs and by inclusion in bespoke credit indices. Volumes are much smaller than foreign CGB holdings — typically CNY 100–300 billion — reflecting lower index inclusion and higher credit-analysis burden for offshore investors.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a higher-beta counterpart to foreign CGB holdings. Foreign commercial-bank bond flows tend to be more volatile and more sensitive to China credit spread moves than sovereign flows. A divergence — foreign investors selling bank bonds while holding CGBs — signals growing concern about bank balance-sheet quality (e.g., property-loan exposure). Pair with aCNHSFIGNA and aCNBDCMBNA for a complete picture of foreign positioning across the credit spectrum.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Foreign Investors - Credit Asset Backed Securities
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Foreign Investors / ABS
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond series measuring foreign investors' holdings of credit ABS in the Chinese interbank bond market. Foreign ABS holdings are small relative to CGBs — typically below CNY 50 billion — because structured products require deeper local legal and credit analysis, and most ABS tranches lack ratings recognised by global index providers. Growth has been gradual since regulators opened the credit-ABS market to foreign investors via Bond Connect expansion.
rics.how_to_use: A niche indicator most relevant for tracking the internationalisation of China's securitisation market. Rising foreign ABS holdings signal improving investor confidence in Chinese structured-credit legal frameworks and collateral transparency. For macro analysts it is most useful in the context of the aggregate foreign holdings picture alongside aCNHSFIGNA and aCNHSFIPNA — the ABS component is small enough that large swings likely reflect technical rather than macro-driven positioning.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Foreign Investors - Enterprise Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Foreign Investors / Enterprise Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond statistic for foreign investors' holdings of enterprise bonds (NDRC-approved corporate bonds issued by state-linked entities). Foreign holdings of enterprise bonds are minimal — often below CNY 20 billion — due to the heterogeneous issuer base, limited secondary market liquidity, and ongoing LGFV debt-restructuring risk. The series provides a lower bound on foreign engagement with China's credit markets beyond policy-bank paper.
rics.how_to_use: Primarily a stress indicator: if foreign holdings of enterprise bonds decline sharply, it often reflects hedging of China credit risk broadly and may coincide with spread widening in LGFV-linked paper. Analysts covering onshore credit spreads should pair this with aCNBDETBNA (total enterprise bond depository stock) to measure the foreign share. An extremely low foreign share (sub-1%) confirms enterprise bonds remain a domestic institutional market.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Foreign Investors - Local Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Foreign Investors / Local Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond data capturing foreign investors' holdings of Chinese local government bonds (LGBs). LGBs are the largest single bond category by outstanding (~CNY 50+ trillion), but foreign holdings are negligible — typically below CNY 100 billion — due to limited index inclusion, heterogeneous credit profiles across 31 provinces, and unresolved LGFV contingent-liability concerns. The series documents the still-early internationalisation of this market segment.
rics.how_to_use: Monitor for inflection points that would signal broadening foreign access to China's sub-sovereign debt market. A material increase in foreign LGB holdings would imply improved index inclusion (e.g., dedicated Bloomberg China Local Government sub-index), and would reduce the effective cost of sub-sovereign borrowing by broadening the investor base. Pair with aCNHSTCLNA (total LGB holdings) to compute the foreign share. Currently primarily a gap-monitoring series.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Foreign Investors - Policy Bank Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Foreign Investors / Policy Bank Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond data on foreign holdings of policy bank bonds — bonds issued by China Development Bank (CDB), Agricultural Development Bank of China (ADBC), and Export-Import Bank of China (Eximbank). Policy bank bonds carry quasi-sovereign status, are included in major EM bond indices (e.g., Bloomberg EM Local Currency Government Index), and offer a modest yield premium of 20–40 bps over comparable CGBs. Foreign holdings typically run CNY 200–500 billion.
rics.how_to_use: Policy bank bond holdings are the second pillar of foreign positioning in China fixed income after CGBs. Monitor alongside aCNHSFIGNA to compute total foreign bond holdings; the ratio between the two series (policy bank vs CGB preference) can signal relative-value shifts or index-rebalancing effects. Rising foreign policy-bank bond holdings despite a static or declining CGB share may suggest index-mandated buying of CDB/ADBC paper rather than discretionary macro positioning.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Insurance Insitutions - Local Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Insurance Institutions / Local Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond series tracking local government bond holdings by insurance companies and other insurance institutions. Chinese insurers — including life insurers managing long-duration liabilities — have been major buyers of long-dated LGBs as a duration-matching tool, given the ~30-year issuance tenor available for special-purpose bonds. Insurance sector LGB holdings have grown rapidly as the sector manages asset-liability mismatch under CBIRC solvency II-style regulations.
rics.how_to_use: Key for understanding structural demand for long-duration LGBs. When insurer LGB holdings grow faster than total LGB issuance, it signals duration-driven demand independent of yield moves, helping to explain the flattening of the long end of the yield curve. For liability-driven investment (LDI) analysis, track alongside aCNHSTCLNA and aCNBDLGBNA. Rapid growth here during periods of falling long yields (as in 2024) can reinforce the 'duration trap' dynamic in China's insurance sector.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Inter-bank Market - China Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Inter-bank Market / CGBs
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond statistic measuring the total stock of Chinese Government Bonds held within the China Interbank Bond Market (CIBM). The CIBM accounts for approximately 95% of all CGB trading and depository volume; this series essentially captures all CGB holdings by CIBM participants including commercial banks, policy banks, funds, insurance companies, and foreign investors. It is closely related to aCNBDCGBNA and serves as the interbank sub-aggregate of total depository.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the primary benchmark for total CGB market depth. The interbank share of CGB holdings shows how much of the sovereign bond market is held in the OTC interbank system versus the exchange (SSE/SZSE); a stable or rising interbank share confirms CIBM dominance. Cross with individual investor-type holdings (commercial banks, foreign investors, insurance) to decompose the demand structure. Rapid overall growth reflects fiscal expansion and large-scale government bond issuance.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Inter-bank Market - Foreign Investors
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Inter-bank Market / Foreign Investors
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond data capturing the total bond holdings of foreign investors within the CIBM across all bond types. This aggregates foreign holdings of CGBs, policy bank bonds, commercial bank bonds, enterprise bonds, and ABS into a single interbank foreign-investor subtotal. It is the primary measure of total foreign fixed-income positioning in China's onshore market, published by ChinaBond monthly.
rics.how_to_use: This is the most comprehensive monthly measure of foreign bond positioning in China. Use it as the top-line foreign-flow indicator: month-over-month changes in this series are the closest available proxy to net portfolio bond inflows from the financial account. Declining totals in 2022–24 tracked the CGB-UST spread compression and served as a leading indicator of CNY depreciation pressure. Pair with aCNXRUSD and aCNHSFIGNA to decompose sovereign vs credit-driven outflows.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Other Markets - China Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Other Markets / CGBs
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond series for Chinese Government Bonds held in markets outside the main CIBM — primarily the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) and Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SZSE) bond platforms, which cater to retail and smaller institutional investors. Exchange-listed CGBs are smaller in size and less liquid than CIBM-cleared equivalents; their yields can diverge modestly from CIBM prices due to different investor bases and trading mechanisms.
rics.how_to_use: Use this series to monitor the exchange-market component of total CGB demand. A rising 'Other Markets' CGB share may signal retail investor demand for safe assets (flight-to-quality during equity sell-offs) or PBoC-directed expansion of retail CGB access. Compare with aCNHSIBGNA to see the CIBM vs exchange split. Exchange-held CGBs are less influenced by institutional flows and can diverge from CIBM yields during periods of retail-driven demand spikes.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Other Markets - Credit Asset Backed Securities
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Other Markets / ABS
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond data on credit ABS held in non-CIBM markets, primarily the SSE and SZSE exchange-listed ABS market (asset-backed notes, ABN, and exchange-traded ABS). Exchange-listed ABS is a separate regulatory channel from interbank credit ABS and is supervised by CSRC rather than PBOC; it includes consumer finance ABS, real estate ABS, and infrastructure REITs precursors. This series captures that non-interbank component.
rics.how_to_use: Cross with aCNHCABTOA (total ABS holdings across all investors) and aCNBDCASNA (interbank ABS depository) to quantify the exchange vs interbank split in China's ABS market. A growing exchange-market ABS share signals CSRC-supervised securitisation gaining ground, often associated with retail-accessible products. Analysts tracking China's infrastructure REIT pipeline should monitor this series as a proxy for exchange-traded structured product development.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Securities Companies - Credit Asset Backed Securities
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Securities Companies / ABS
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond series for credit ABS held by securities companies (broker-dealers). Securities firms hold ABS primarily in their proprietary trading books and asset management products (AMPs). Their ABS holdings tend to be concentrated in mezzanine and junior tranches where returns are higher, reflecting their risk appetite and shorter liability structure compared with banks and insurers.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a risk-appetite barometer for China's broker-dealer community. Rising securities company ABS holdings coincide with risk-on conditions in credit markets; falling holdings often precede spread widening as dealers reduce risk. Pair with aCNHCABTOA and aCNHCABCBA (state-bank ABS holdings) to contrast risk-seeking vs risk-averse investor behaviour within the ABS market. Sharp drops can also signal regulatory tightening on brokerage leverage or AMP restrictions.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Total - China Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond aggregate of Chinese Government Bond holdings across all investor categories and markets. This is the total outstanding depository stock of CGBs by holder — essentially the demand-side counterpart to the issuance series aCNISCGBNA and the supply-side series aCNBDCGBNA. Published approximately 10–15 business days after month-end. With total CGBs outstanding above CNY 30 trillion as of 2024–25, this is a critical macro-scale series.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the denominator when computing individual investor-type shares (e.g., foreign share = aCNHSFIGNA / aCNHSTCGNA). Month-on-month growth directly reflects net CGB issuance absorbed by the market. Analysts can decompose whether fiscal expansion is being funded by domestic banks (risk-recycling) or by genuine diversification across insurance and foreign investors. The 2024 historic CGB rally to 1.6% yields is visible in issuance surges tracked by this series alongside aCNISCGBNA.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Total - Credit Asset Backed Securities
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond aggregate of credit asset-backed securities held by all investor categories combined. Encompasses holdings in both CIBM and exchange markets. China's credit ABS market has grown from near-zero pre-2012 to over CNY 3 trillion outstanding by the mid-2020s, with auto-loan and corporate-loan ABS dominating. This total-market view is published alongside the investor-breakdown sub-series in the ChinaBond monthly statistical release.
rics.how_to_use: Provides the total-market context for interpreting investor-specific ABS holding series (e.g., aCNHCABCBA, aCNHCABJCA). Rising totals confirm a healthy primary-market ABS pipeline; stagnant or declining totals may signal originator stress (e.g., reduced loan origination at banks) or investor demand withdrawal. Use the year-on-year growth rate alongside aCNBIABSNA (new issuance) and aCNIPABSCA (interest payments) to build a comprehensive ABS market accounting.

rics.description: Bond Holding Structure: Total - Local Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Holding Structure — Total / Local Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond aggregate of local government bond holdings across all investor types. LGBs are China's largest bond category by outstanding (~CNY 50 trillion+ as of 2025), comprising general-purpose bonds and special-purpose bonds (SPBs) used to fund infrastructure, public housing, and debt refinancing. Commercial banks hold the vast majority (~80%), with insurers and funds holding most of the remainder. Foreign holdings remain marginal.
rics.how_to_use: Track total LGB depository growth as the primary measure of the build-up of sub-sovereign debt in China's bond market. Rapid growth — as seen in 2023–25 with large special-bond quotas — raises questions about implicit fiscal pressure on the banking system when banks absorb most issuance. The growth rate of this series relative to nominal GDP growth is a key long-run fiscal sustainability metric. Pair with aCNBDLGBNA (ChinaBond depository version) and aCNISCGBNA (central government issuance) for fiscal decomposition.

rics.description: Bond Issuance: China Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly issuance volume of Chinese Government Bonds in CNY terms, as reported by the Ministry of Finance and compiled by Refinitiv/ChinaBond. CGBs are direct obligations of the central government, issued across a full curve from 3 months to 50 years; the 10-year CGB is China's benchmark sovereign rate. Gross monthly issuance runs CNY 400–900 billion, reflecting both new supply and rollover of maturing bonds. The 'CA' suffix typically denotes the yuan-denominated current-price series.
rics.how_to_use: Critical for tracking fiscal stance: a surge in CGB issuance signals expanded deficit financing or front-loaded fiscal stimulus. Subtract principal repayments (available via aCNPPCBBNA for CBBs as a proxy) from gross issuance to estimate net issuance. Combine with aCNISGABNA (agency bond issuance) for total sovereign + quasi-sovereign supply. Large issuance can push up short-term repo rates if bank reserve absorption is insufficient; monitor alongside PBoC OMO data for liquidity management responses.

rics.description: Bond Issuance: China Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly face-value issuance volume of Chinese Government Bonds, the notional/volume counterpart to aCNISCGBCA. The distinction between 'NA' (notional amount) and 'CA' (current prices) series reflects that bonds may be issued at a premium or discount to par. Published monthly by the Ministry of Finance with a brief lag and compiled into Refinitiv's China macro database. This is the standard issuance series used for supply-side fiscal analysis.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the primary CGB supply indicator. Year-to-date cumulative issuance versus the annual quota (set in the government work report each March NPC) is watched closely for fiscal execution pace. A front-loaded issuance profile (heavy H1 supply) is bearish for short-term rates as banks must absorb large volumes; back-loaded issuance into Q4 is rarer and often signals fiscal shortfalls. Cross with aCNBDCGBNA (depository outstanding) to track the rolling stock of CGB debt.

rics.description: Bond Issuance: Government-backed Agency Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly issuance volume of government-backed agency bonds, which in the Chinese context primarily encompasses policy bank bonds issued by China Development Bank (CDB), Agricultural Development Bank of China (ADBC), and the Export-Import Bank of China. These bonds carry implicit government backing, are zero-risk-weighted for bank capital purposes, and typically yield 20–50 bps above comparable CGBs. Combined outstanding exceeds CNY 25 trillion, making policy banks the largest non-sovereign bond issuer in Asia.
rics.how_to_use: Policy bank issuance is a key quasi-fiscal tool: CDB bond proceeds fund infrastructure and housing projects (pledged supplementary lending, PSL), while ADBC funds agricultural support. Rising aCNISGABNA issuance often accompanies infrastructure stimulus packages. The spread between CDB 10Y and CGB 10Y (CDB-CGB spread) narrows when policy banks have strong demand and widens under supply pressure. Use alongside aCNBDGABNA and aCNBSGACNA to track the full policy-bank bond lifecycle.

rics.description: Bond Principal Payment: Central Bank Bills
rics.subcategory: Bond Principal Payment — Central Bank Bills
rics.meaning: Monthly principal repayments on People's Bank of China (PBoC) bills (央行票据). Central bank bills were a major liquidity sterilisation instrument used heavily from 2003 to 2013 to absorb excess reserves generated by large forex inflows. PBoC stopped net issuance of domestic CBBs around 2013–14 as forex inflows slowed, but still occasionally issues offshore CNY CBBs in Hong Kong to manage CNH liquidity. This series tracks scheduled redemptions of the residual outstanding stock.
rics.how_to_use: Monitor as an automatic liquidity injection signal: CBB maturities return principal to the banking system without requiring PBoC action. In periods with a residual CBB stock, large redemptions can ease money-market conditions and put modest downward pressure on repo rates. Today the stock is very small, making the series primarily of historical and structural interest. Pair with aCNBDCBBNA (depository outstanding of CBBs) to track the remaining stock and its scheduled runoff.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Central Bank Bills
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository Outstanding — Central Bank Bills
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of outstanding PBoC central bank bills registered at the central clearing system. At its peak around 2008, the CBB stock exceeded CNY 4 trillion as the PBoC sterilised USD reserve inflows. Following the shift in China's balance-of-payments dynamics post-2014, the domestic CBB stock fell to near-zero. Residual amounts primarily reflect offshore CNY CBBs (issued in HK to manage CNH liquidity) or legacy instruments.
rics.how_to_use: Primarily a historical and structural series now. A revival in CBB issuance and rising depository stock would signal a major shift in PBoC sterilisation strategy, likely in response to renewed large-scale FX intervention. For current monetary operations analysis, focus instead on PBoC OMO (7-day reverse repos, MLF) as the primary tools. Track aCNPPCBBNA alongside this series to reconcile principal repayments against the remaining stock.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: China Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository Outstanding — China Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of outstanding Chinese Government Bonds — the total face value of all CGBs registered at China Central Depository & Clearing Co., Ltd. (ChinaBond). This is the supply-side accumulated-stock series: it grows each month by net CGB issuance minus redemptions. As of 2024–25, total CGB outstanding exceeds CNY 30 trillion, making it the world's second-largest sovereign bond market after U.S. Treasuries. Published monthly by ChinaBond with a short lag.
rics.how_to_use: The foundational CGB market-size series. Divide by GDP for debt-to-GDP tracking; compute month-on-month change to approximate net CGB issuance. Use as the denominator for computing foreign, bank, and insurance investor shares. Growth acceleration typically coincides with fiscal stimulus (as in 2023–24 CNY 1 trillion special CGB issuance). Analysts using aCNHSTCGNA (total holdings) as a double-check should find near-identical values, since depository = sum of all holdings.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Commercial Bank Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository Outstanding — Commercial Bank Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of commercial bank bonds — financial bonds, Tier-2 capital instruments, perpetual bonds, and negotiable certificates of deposit (NCD) issued by commercial banks and registered at ChinaBond. Chinese banks are major bond issuers: large state-owned banks issue Tier-2 and AT1 perpetuals for capital purposes, while smaller banks rely heavily on NCD issuance for short-term funding. Total commercial bank bond stock exceeds CNY 10 trillion.
rics.how_to_use: Track as an indicator of bank funding stress and capital adequacy cycle. Rising commercial bank bond issuance (and depository growth) can signal: (1) capital rebuilding after loan losses, (2) replacement of retail deposits with wholesale funding, or (3) NCD issuance arbitrage when NCD rates are below benchmark rates. Pair with aCNHSFICNA (foreign holdings of bank bonds) for international demand signals. A divergence between NCD issuance growth and bank deposit growth is a classic banking-system liquidity indicator.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Credit Asset Backed Securities
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of credit asset-backed securities (ABS) registered at the central interbank clearing system. China's interbank ABS market — supervised by PBOC and regulated jointly with CBIRC — covers auto-loan ABS, corporate-loan CLOs, credit-card ABS, and residential mortgage-backed securities (RMBS). Outstanding has grown from near-zero pre-2012 to over CNY 3 trillion by the mid-2020s, driven by bank balance-sheet management needs.
rics.how_to_use: Key for tracking the development of China's securitisation market. Growing depository ABS stock signals banks are actively using off-balance-sheet tools to manage capital ratios and loan concentrations. Stagnation or decline can reflect originator funding constraints or regulatory cooling. Pair with aCNBIABSNA (monthly new issuance) and aCNHCABTOA (holdings by investor type) to build a complete ABS market flow-stock accounting. Monitor relative to total bond market (aCNBDTOTNA) to track ABS share of the overall market.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Enterprise Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of enterprise bonds (企业债) — NDRC-approved bonds historically issued by state-owned enterprises and local government financing vehicles (LGFVs) for infrastructure funding. Enterprise bonds were the dominant corporate bond format before PBOC-supervised MTNs and CSRC-supervised corporate bonds emerged post-2008. Outstanding has declined relative to other categories as issuers migrated to MTNs, but the legacy LGFV stock creates systemic risk concerns.
rics.how_to_use: The enterprise bond outstanding is a proxy for the LGFV debt stock embedded in the public bond market. Rising outstanding relative to nominal GDP growth can signal deteriorating debt serviceability for LGFVs. Use alongside aCNHSCCENA (credit cooperative holdings) and aCNBSETCNA (CIBM settlement volumes for enterprise bonds) to assess liquidity and investor demand conditions. The 2023–24 LGFV debt-swap programme (local government special refinancing bonds) caused a visible decline in this series as LGFV bonds were retired.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Government-backed Agency Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository Outstanding — Government-backed Agency Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of government-backed agency bonds, predominantly policy bank bonds issued by CDB, ADBC, and Eximbank. These bonds are China's largest non-CGB bond category, with combined outstanding exceeding CNY 25 trillion. They carry zero risk weight for bank capital calculations and are included in major bond indices including the Bloomberg China Aggregate Index. ChinaBond publishes this stock monthly, reflecting the rolling balance of issued minus redeemed policy bank paper.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the baseline for quasi-sovereign supply in China. Rising CDB bond outstanding tracks the PBoC's pledged supplementary lending (PSL) programme for shanty-town redevelopment and housing rental — a key fiscal-monetary coordination tool. The spread between policy bank bond yields and CGB yields (20–50 bps typically) is a liquid credit spread benchmark for China fixed income. Pair with aCNISGABNA (monthly new issuance) and aCNBSGACNA (CIBM trading volumes) for a full policy-bank market picture.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Local Government Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository Outstanding — Local Government Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of local government bonds (地方政府债). LGBs — divided into general bonds (funded by general fiscal revenue) and special-purpose bonds (funded by project cash flows) — are now the single largest bond category in China with outstanding exceeding CNY 50 trillion. The annual special-bond quota (set by NPC) has risen sharply from CNY 1.35 trillion (2019) to CNY 4+ trillion (2024–25), making LGB issuance a primary fiscal stimulus lever.
rics.how_to_use: The best single series for tracking China's sub-sovereign debt expansion. Monthly changes approximate net LGB issuance; compare to the announced annual quota to assess fiscal execution pace. Analysts tracking local government debt sustainability should normalise this by provincial GDP and fiscal revenue. The composition (general vs special bonds) matters: special bonds are off-budget by design but create contingent liabilities. Pair with aCNHSTCLNA (holdings breakdown) to see who absorbs issuance.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Non-bank Financial Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository Outstanding — Non-bank Financial Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of bonds issued by non-bank financial institutions — including securities companies, trust companies, finance companies of corporate groups, and consumer finance firms. These bonds fund short-term wholesale operations and medium-term balance-sheet growth at NBFIs. The category is distinct from bank-issued financial bonds; it is a smaller but growing segment as China's shadow banking sector has shifted toward more formally regulated bond issuance.
rics.how_to_use: Monitor as a gauge of the wholesale funding health of China's non-bank financial sector. Rapid growth in NBFI bond outstanding may signal leveraged expansion in securities or trust lending; stagnation or contraction can signal regulatory tightening (as seen during the asset management regulation reforms of 2017–18). Pair with aCNBINFICP (monthly new issuance of NBFI bonds) and aCNBSNFCNA (CIBM settlement volumes) to build an issuance-trading-outstanding picture.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Others
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond residual category capturing bonds deposited at the central clearing system that do not fall into the standard classification buckets (CGBs, LGBs, policy bank bonds, commercial bank bonds, enterprise bonds, ABS, non-bank financial bonds, or central bank bills). This category includes international development institution bonds (e.g., bonds issued by ADB, World Bank in CNY — panda bonds registered here), subordinated debt, and other niche instruments.
rics.how_to_use: Primarily a balancing series; watch for unusual spikes that might indicate reclassification of instruments between categories or growth in niche bond types. If panda bond issuance is strong, this 'Others' category may grow as some panda bonds are registered at ChinaBond rather than Shanghai Clearing House. Cross-check against the Shanghai Clearing House panda bond series (aCNBIPDBNA) to reconcile the two registries. Generally used to verify that individual category sums add up to aCNBDTOTNA.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Policy Bank Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository Outstanding — Policy Bank Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly ChinaBond depository stock of policy bank bonds (政策性银行债) — bonds issued by CDB, ADBC, and Eximbank registered at ChinaBond. This is the ChinaBond-registry version of the outstanding stock, closely related to aCNBDGABNA (government-backed agency bonds) but focused specifically on the three policy banks. CDB alone accounts for the majority (over CNY 15 trillion) of the total. Policy bank bonds are the most liquid non-CGB instrument in the CIBM.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the base for computing the CDB/policy bank yield curve (available for 1Y, 3Y, 5Y, 7Y, 10Y tenors). Rising outstanding combined with flat or falling yields indicates strong demand from banks, insurers, and foreign investors; stagnant outstanding with rising yields signals supply indigestion. Policy bank bond settlement volumes (aCNBSPBCNA, aCNBSPBOCA) divided by outstanding gives a turnover ratio useful for tracking secondary-market liquidity.

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Total, Current Prices, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, China Central Depository & Clearing Co., Ltd.
rics.meaning: Monthly total bond depository stock at China Central Depository & Clearing Co., Ltd. (ChinaBond) — the sum of all bond categories registered in the ChinaBond system at current prices. This is one of the two broadest measures of the Chinese bond market's size (the other being aCNBDTOTNP in volume terms). ChinaBond manages the central registry for CGBs, LGBs, policy bank bonds, and financial bonds; Shanghai Clearing House manages MTNs, CP, panda bonds, and most ABS. The two registries combined give the full onshore bond market.
rics.how_to_use: The flagship size indicator for the ChinaBond-registered portion of China's bond market. Use it as the market-cap denominator for computing individual category shares. Combine with the Shanghai Clearing House equivalents (aCNBCMTNCA, aCNBCCMPCA, aCNBCFIBNA) for a near-complete total bond market estimate. Year-on-year growth relative to GDP and M2 growth provides a useful measure of financial deepening. This series shows China's bond market growing from ~CNY 80 trillion (2019) to over CNY 130 trillion (2024).

rics.description: Bonds Depository Outstanding: Total, Volume, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, China Central Depository & Clearing Co., Ltd.
rics.meaning: Monthly total bond depository stock at ChinaBond in face-value (notional) terms — the volume counterpart to aCNBDTOTNA which uses current prices. For bonds trading at premium or discount to par, the two series will diverge slightly. Face-value totals are more commonly used for debt-outstanding analysis because they reflect principal repayment obligations; price-based totals are used for market-value or mark-to-market assessments. Published simultaneously with aCNBDTOTNA by ChinaBond.
rics.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNBDTOTNA for market-value vs face-value comparisons. In a bull bond market (2023–24), bonds trade above par so aCNBDTOTNA > aCNBDTOTNP; in a bear market the opposite holds. The divergence is a crude measure of aggregate market-to-par premium. For debt sustainability and fiscal analysis, use aCNBDTOTNP (face value) as the relevant liability measure. Both series are available for individual bond categories enabling category-level price/par comparisons.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Central Bank Bills - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Central Bank Bills (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly CIBM cash-bond settlement volume for PBoC central bank bills. Cash bond settlements (现券交易) represent outright buy/sell transactions in the secondary market, as opposed to repo transactions. With the CBB stock near zero, settlement volumes are negligible. This series is primarily of historical interest, capturing the period when CBBs were actively traded as the dominant PBoC sterilisation instrument during 2003–2013. ChinaBond publishes this as part of its monthly CIBM settlement statistics.
rics.how_to_use: Negligible in the current market context. Historical data (2003–2013) provides insight into how China's central bank managed liquidity during the massive foreign-exchange accumulation era. If PBoC ever revives domestic CBB issuance as a sterilisation tool, this series would again become relevant. Use aCNBDCBBNA (outstanding) and aCNPPCBBNA (repayments) as the companion series for tracking the residual CBB lifecycle.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: China Government Bonds - Cash Bond
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond settlement volume for Chinese Government Bonds in the China Interbank Bond Market. This measures secondary-market trading activity — outright buy/sell transactions — in CGBs by CIBM participants. CGB cash-bond settlement is the most liquid segment of China's bond market; daily volumes can exceed CNY 200–400 billion in active periods. ChinaBond publishes monthly aggregates as part of its interbank bond market statistics.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the primary CGB secondary-market liquidity indicator. Monthly turnover ratio (settlement volume / aCNBDCGBNA outstanding) shows how actively the market is trading. Elevated settlement volumes coincide with rate volatility, PBoC operations, or index-rebalancing events. Declining settlement volumes relative to outstanding suggest reduced market liquidity — a warning sign for foreign investors using Bond Connect, who depend on secondary-market depth for position management. Cross with aCNBSPBCNA (policy bank cash bonds) for relative-liquidity comparison.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Commercial Bank Bonds - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Commercial Bank Bonds (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond settlement volume for commercial bank bonds (financial bonds and NCDs) in the CIBM. This captures secondary-market trading in bank-issued debt instruments, which is an important gauge of wholesale funding market liquidity. NCD (negotiable certificate of deposit) secondary trading is included here, making this series particularly sensitive to interbank funding conditions and money-market spreads.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a proxy for wholesale bank funding market conditions. High commercial bank bond settlement volume indicates active NCD and financial bond trading — liquid conditions; low volume suggests bid-offer spreads have widened and funding is constrained. A spike in settlement volume often accompanies bank stress events (e.g., credit events at smaller banks) as holders sell down positions. Pair with aCNBDCMBNA (outstanding) for turnover analysis and aCNBSCGCNA for relative-liquidity benchmarking against CGBs.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Credit Asset Backed Securities - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Credit ABS (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond settlement volume for credit asset-backed securities in the interbank bond market. ABS secondary-market liquidity is materially lower than for CGBs or policy bank bonds — most ABS tranches are held to maturity by banks and insurers. Monthly settlement volumes are a fraction of the outstanding stock, reflecting the buy-and-hold investor base and the complexity of ABS pricing. ChinaBond publishes this as part of CIBM market statistics.
rics.how_to_use: The low turnover ratio (settlement / outstanding) for credit ABS versus CGBs quantifies the secondary-market illiquidity premium embedded in ABS yields. Rising ABS cash-bond settlement signals improved secondary-market liquidity, which would lower new-issuance yields by reducing the illiquidity discount. For structured credit investors, compare aCNBSCACNA to aCNBDCASNA (outstanding) to derive a monthly turnover ratio — a structural indicator of ABS market development.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Enterprise Bonds - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Enterprise Bonds (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond settlement volume for enterprise bonds (NDRC corporate bonds, largely LGFV) in the CIBM. Enterprise bond secondary-market liquidity is thin — most LGFV bonds are illiquid, with limited price discovery. Settlement volumes here provide a lower bound on active secondary trading; structural holders (banks, trust products) rarely trade. A sudden spike in settlement volume can indicate distress-driven selling or regulatory pressure to reduce LGFV exposure.
rics.how_to_use: Enterprise bond settlement volume is an early warning indicator for LGFV credit stress. Monitor alongside aCNBDETBNA (outstanding stock): if settlement surges while outstanding is static or declining, it signals investors offloading positions. During China's 2023–24 LGFV debt-swap programmes, enterprise bond settlements picked up as local governments redeemed LGFV bonds using special refinancing bonds, creating unusual trading activity. Pair with aCNHSCCENA (credit cooperative holdings) for a buyer/seller flow picture.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Foreign Investors - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Foreign Investors (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly CIBM cash-bond settlement volume attributed to foreign investor transactions — the trading-activity complement to the holdings series (aCNHSIFINA). This series captures how actively foreign investors are buying and selling bonds in the CIBM, as recorded by ChinaBond. It covers transactions via Bond Connect (northbound), CIBM Direct, and QFII/RQFII channels. Published monthly as part of ChinaBond's CIBM market statistics.
rics.how_to_use: Distinguish between foreign 'holding' (stock) changes and foreign 'activity' (flow). A month where foreign settlement volume is high but holdings are unchanged suggests two-way trading without net direction — a healthy sign. When settlement volume falls alongside falling holdings, it indicates outright exit. A high turnover ratio (foreign settlement / foreign holdings via aCNHSIFINA) measures foreign investor engagement — a rising ratio signals active portfolio management versus passive buy-and-hold. Pair with aCNBSCGCNA (total CGB cash bond settlement) to compute the foreign share of CGB trading.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Government-backed Agency Bonds - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Government-backed Agency Bonds (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond settlement volume for government-backed agency bonds (policy bank bonds) in the CIBM. Policy bank bonds — CDB, ADBC, Eximbank — are the second most actively traded instrument after CGBs in the Chinese interbank market; their secondary-market liquidity is high due to large outstanding sizes and broad investor base. CDB 10Y bonds serve as the benchmark quasi-sovereign rate. Monthly settlement volumes can reach CNY 500+ billion in active periods.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a policy bank bond liquidity indicator. The policy bank bond turnover ratio (aCNBSGACNA / aCNBDGABNA) is a key relative-liquidity metric — typically lower than CGBs but higher than most credit bonds. When the CDB-CGB spread widens, settlement volumes often rise as investors engage in relative-value trades between the two sectors. Combine with aCNBSPBCNA (cash bond) and aCNBSPBOCA (outright repo) for a comprehensive view of policy bank bond secondary-market activity.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Local Government Bonds - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Local Government Bonds (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond settlement volume for local government bonds in the China Interbank Bond Market. Despite LGBs being the largest bond category by outstanding (~CNY 50 trillion+), secondary-market liquidity is poor: most LGBs are held to maturity by commercial banks, creating very low turnover ratios. Secondary trading is episodic, typically triggered by LGB-related repo transactions or index-rebalancing rather than price-driven active management.
rics.how_to_use: The key insight from this series is the contrast between LGB outstanding size and trading activity: a very low turnover ratio (aCNBSLGCNA / aCNBDLGBNA) confirms LGBs are quasi-illiquid instruments despite their scale. Any sustained increase in LGB secondary settlement would signal a structural improvement in market liquidity — perhaps from expanded Bond Connect eligibility or ChinaBond repo-collateral status changes. For fiscal analysis, focus on aCNBDLGBNA (stock) and aCNHSTCLNA (holdings) rather than settlement.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Non-bank Financial Bonds - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Non-bank Financial Bonds (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond settlement volume for non-bank financial institution bonds in the CIBM. NBFI bonds (issued by securities firms, trust companies, consumer finance companies) are generally less liquid than bank financial bonds or policy bank bonds. Settlement volumes reflect both proprietary trading by securities companies and limited institutional investor activity. Volatility in NBFI bond settlement can signal sector-level funding stress.
rics.how_to_use: Monitor as a secondary-market liquidity barometer for China's non-bank financial sector. Declining settlement volumes in NBFI bonds alongside rising yields is an early-warning signal of funding stress for securities companies or trust firms. Cross with aCNBDNFBNA (outstanding) to compute turnover, and with aCNBINFICP (new issuance) to see whether the primary market is functioning. Sharp drops in NBFI bond liquidity can foreshadow broader credit events in the shadow banking system.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Others - Cash Bond
rics.meaning: Monthly residual cash-bond settlement volume in the CIBM for bond categories not captured in the standard sector breakdowns. This includes subordinated debt, international organisation bonds, panda bonds settled via ChinaBond, and other niche instruments. Like the depository 'Others' category (aCNBDOTHNA), this is a balancing item that ensures settlement volume breakdowns sum to the total (aCNBSTOCNA).
rics.how_to_use: Use as a consistency check: the sum of all CIBM bond settlement sector series should equal aCNBSTOCNA. If the 'Others' component is large relative to total settlement, it may indicate a growing niche segment (e.g., panda bonds, subordinated debt) gaining secondary-market traction. Useful for tracking the early-stage development of instruments before they receive their own dedicated breakdown series. Monitor alongside aCNBIPDBNA (panda bond issuance) for correlation.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Policy Bank Bonds - Cash Bond
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Policy Bank Bonds (Cash Bond)
rics.meaning: Monthly cash-bond (outright purchase/sale) settlement volume for policy bank bonds (CDB, ADBC, Eximbank) in the CIBM. Policy bank bonds are among the most actively traded instruments in China's bond market, with CDB 10Y bonds serving as the key benchmark for the quasi-sovereign rate. Cash-bond settlement volumes here reflect pure secondary-market trading activity, distinct from repo-backed transactions captured in aCNBSPBOCA.
rics.how_to_use: The CDB cash-bond turnover ratio (aCNBSPBCNA / aCNBDPBBNA) is a key liquidity quality indicator. When CDB-CGB spread compression drives relative-value demand, cash-bond settlement volumes spike; spread widening typically accompanies declining volumes as market makers widen bid-offer spreads. For foreign investors holding policy bank bonds via Bond Connect or CIBM Direct, high cash-bond settlement volumes are critical for exit liquidity. Pair with aCNBSPBOCA (repo volumes) to distinguish outright trading from financing activity.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Policy Bank Bonds - Outright Repo
rics.subcategory: CIBM Bond Settlement — Policy Bank Bonds (Outright Repo)
rics.meaning: Monthly outright repo settlement volume for policy bank bonds in the CIBM. Outright repos (买断式回购) are structured as true sales with a forward repurchase commitment — a key tool for leveraged bond positions and short-selling in China's bond market. They differ from pledged repos (质押式回购) which are more common for collateralised funding. Policy bank bonds are preferred outright repo collateral due to their liquidity and low credit risk.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNBSPBCNA (cash bond) to compute the repo-to-outright ratio for policy bank bonds: a high ratio indicates leveraged positioning or hedging activity. Rising outright repo volumes in policy bank bonds signal that participants are using CDB/ADBC bonds as leverage vehicles — typical in carry-trade environments with steep repo-to-bond yield curves. A sudden drop can precede deleveraging. Also used by PBoC as a signal for systemic leverage in the bond market.

rics.description: CIBM Bond Settlement: Total - Cash Bond
rics.meaning: Monthly total cash-bond settlement volume in the China Interbank Bond Market across all bond categories. This is the broadest measure of secondary-market trading activity in China's OTC bond market. Total CIBM cash-bond settlement typically runs CNY 2–5 trillion per month, dwarfing exchange-listed bond trading. Published by ChinaBond monthly, this series aggregates settlement across CGBs, LGBs, policy bank bonds, commercial bank bonds, enterprise bonds, ABS, and other categories.
rics.how_to_use: The total cash-bond settlement series is the top-level CIBM liquidity indicator. Year-on-year changes reflect shifts in overall market depth and activity. Declining total settlement relative to outstanding (aCNBDTOTNA) signals market liquidity deterioration, raising transaction costs and reducing price discovery quality. Use as the denominator for computing sector-level settlement shares (e.g., CGB settlement as % of total = aCNBSCGCNA / aCNBSTOCNA). Surges in total settlement often coincide with PBoC interest rate operations or fiscal policy announcements.

rics.description: Overview:  Bond Issuance
rics.meaning: Monthly overview aggregate of total bond issuance across all categories in China's bond market, compiled by ChinaBond. This top-line issuance series covers CGB, LGB, policy bank bonds, commercial bank bonds (including NCDs), enterprise bonds, ABS, MTNs, commercial paper, panda bonds, and other instruments. Monthly gross issuance regularly exceeds CNY 5–8 trillion (including NCD rollover), making the Chinese primary bond market one of the world's most active.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the headline indicator of primary market activity. Month-on-month changes track the pace of bond supply; year-on-year comparisons reveal structural trends in bond financing relative to bank loan growth. In periods of PBoC easing, issuance typically accelerates as lower yields incentivise borrowers; in tightening, issuance can slow. Combine with aCNBRTOTNA (redemptions) to compute net issuance — the true increment to bond market debt. The mix between issuance types (sovereign, credit, structured) reveals funding-source shifts.

rics.description: Overview:  Bond Issuance
rics.units: Number of issuances or CNY billion (volume)
rics.meaning: Monthly overview bond issuance series — the count or volume counterpart to aCNOVBISNA. The 'CA' suffix may denote either a count-of-transactions variant or a separate currency/price-basis variant of the total issuance overview. Published by ChinaBond as part of the standard monthly bond market overview. This series alongside aCNOVBISNA provides complementary perspectives on issuance — size vs frequency of bond sales.
rics.how_to_use: Use the count series (if that is the measurement) to compute average deal size: falling average deal size amid high total count can signal fragmentation of the primary market toward smaller, lower-quality issuers. If both volume and count are growing, the market is deepening broadly. For relative analysis, compare count-based issuance trends with aCNBITOTNP (Shanghai Clearing House total issuance volume) to see whether the two major registry systems are growing in tandem.

rics.description: Overview:  Bond Settlement - Tri-party Repo
rics.subcategory: Bond Market Overview — Tri-party Repo Settlement
rics.meaning: Monthly tri-party repo settlement volume in China's bond market. Tri-party repos (三方回购) — administered via Shanghai Clearing House with a tri-party agent managing collateral — are a growing segment of the Chinese repo market, offering more standardised collateral management than bilateral pledged repos. They became more prominent after regulatory reforms to reduce counterparty concentration and improve collateral transparency in the interbank funding market.
rics.how_to_use: Monitor tri-party repo volumes as an indicator of collateral management sophistication and interbank funding market development. Rising tri-party repo volumes signal that market participants are moving away from bilateral repos toward more transparent, standardised structures — a positive structural development. Tri-party repo rates often trade close to the 7-day reverse repo benchmark; spikes in volume can indicate increased demand for short-term funding using bond collateral, potentially signalling market stress or seasonal funding pressure.

rics.description: Overview:  Bonds Depository Outstanding
rics.subcategory: Bond Market Overview — Total Depository Outstanding
rics.meaning: Monthly overview total of bond depository outstanding across both major Chinese clearing systems — ChinaBond (China Central Depository & Clearing) and Shanghai Clearing House (上海清算所). This combined total is the most comprehensive measure of China's total onshore bond market size, covering CGBs, LGBs, policy bank bonds, commercial bank bonds, enterprise bonds, MTNs, commercial paper, ABS, panda bonds, and green notes. The combined market exceeded CNY 160 trillion by 2024–25.
rics.how_to_use: The single most comprehensive bond market size indicator for China. Use aCNOVBDONA as the denominator for computing market shares, yield-to-GDP ratios, and internationalisation metrics. Growth rate versus M2 and nominal GDP reveals financial deepening trends. As the overview aggregate, it exceeds aCNBDTOTNA (ChinaBond only) by including Shanghai Clearing House-registered bonds (MTNs, CP, panda bonds, short-term securities company bonds). Use to benchmark China's bond market against other markets (US, Japan, EU).

rics.description: Overview:  Inter-bank Market Investors
rics.subcategory: Bond Market Overview — Inter-bank Market Investors
rics.meaning: Monthly count of registered participants in the China Interbank Bond Market (CIBM). Market participants include commercial banks, policy banks, securities companies, fund management companies, insurance companies, foreign institutional investors (via Bond Connect or CIBM Direct), and other financial institutions. Growing participation signals market opening and deepening; the CIBM investor base has expanded markedly since 2016 as foreign access was broadened via Bond Connect (2017) and FTSE/Bloomberg index inclusion.
rics.how_to_use: Track as a structural market-development indicator. A rising participant count signals broadening market access and improving price discovery from more diverse investors. Specifically monitor growth in foreign investor registration as a measure of bond market internationalisation — accelerating registration ahead of index inclusion events signals anticipatory positioning. For domestic purposes, growth in the number of small/mid-tier bank and NBFI participants signals improved access to the core bond market for wholesale funding.

rics.description: Chinese insurance companies, original insurance premium income, ABC Life
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Life Premium Income / ABC Life
rics.meaning: Monthly original insurance premium income (原保险保费收入) for ABC Life Insurance (农银人寿), a joint-venture life insurer affiliated with Agricultural Bank of China. Published by the National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA, formerly CBIRC) in monthly insurance statistical bulletins. Premium income directly drives investable asset flows into bonds, equities, and alternative investments; life insurers are structurally long-duration bond buyers.
rics.how_to_use: ABC Life's premium income is a micro-level input to the broader insurance sector asset allocation picture. Rapid premium growth at bancassurance-channel insurers (like ABC Life) directly translates to incremental demand for long-duration bonds, especially LGBs and CDB bonds. Aggregate with peer series (aCNCNZTOKM, aCNCNGIFUM) to construct a sectoral insurance inflow indicator. Rising sector-wide premium income is structurally bullish for long-end yields — more insurance money chasing fixed-income assets.

rics.description: Chinese insurance companies, original insurance premium income, Love life
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Life Premium Income / Love Life
rics.meaning: Monthly original insurance premium income for Love Life Insurance (爱心人寿 or similar entity), a smaller Chinese life insurer. Reported by NFRA in the monthly insurance statistical release. This series is one of many company-level premium income series that together constitute the Chinese life insurance sector premium aggregate. Individual company data provides granularity unavailable in sector-level totals.
rics.how_to_use: Individual insurer premium data is primarily used in bottom-up sector analysis — comparing growth rates across carriers reveals market-share shifts between distribution channels (bancassurance, agency, direct). From a bond-market perspective, aggregate premium growth across the sector is more important than any single company; use this alongside aCNCNCJSM and aCNCNGIFUM to build a composite insurer asset-demand signal for long-duration bonds.

rics.description: Chinese personal insurance companies, policyholders new payments, China Ping An Life Insurance
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Life Policyholder New Payments / Ping An Life
rics.meaning: Monthly new policyholder premium payments (新单保费) at China Ping An Life Insurance (平安人寿) — the premium income attributable to newly issued policies rather than renewals. Ping An Life is China's largest life insurer by new-business premium. New-business premium is a leading indicator of future in-force premium income and investable asset growth. Published by NFRA in monthly regulatory statistics.
rics.how_to_use: New policyholder payments at Ping An Life provide a real-time signal for trends in China's savings insurance market. Rising new-business premium at Ping An suggests consumers are rotating from deposits or wealth-management products into guaranteed insurance savings — a structural shift that creates predictable, long-duration demand for bonds. Analysts tracking property insurance sector recovery (post-2022 downturn) should compare this growth with aCNCNJKLPM (Ping An Property) to assess the life vs non-life split within the conglomerate.

rics.description: Chinese personal insurance companies, policyholders new payments, Safe Pension
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Life Policyholder New Payments / Safe Pension
rics.meaning: Monthly new policyholder premium payments at Safe Pension Insurance (平安养老保险 or similar entity), a pension-focused insurer. Pension insurance products in China — primarily managed by life and pension subsidiaries of major groups — are particularly important bond-market participants given the very long-duration liability structure (20–40 years) which drives demand for ultra-long CGBs, 30-year LGBs, and CDB perpetuals.
rics.how_to_use: Pension insurer new premium growth is structurally the most duration-sensitive insurance data series. As China ages demographically, pension insurer assets are expected to become one of the largest pools of long-duration bond demand over the next decade. Use alongside aCNCNGIFUM (Ping An Life) and aCNHSIILNA (total insurance LGB holdings) to track the pension sector's contribution to long-end CGB and LGB demand. Rising pension premium growth is a medium-term bullish signal for 30Y CGB yields.

rics.description: Chinese property insurance companies, premium income, China Coal Property
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Property Premium Income / China Coal Property
rics.meaning: Monthly premium income of China Coal Property & Casualty Insurance (中煤财产保险), a niche property insurer serving the coal and energy sector. Published by NFRA in its monthly property insurance statistical releases. Property insurance premiums are a shorter-duration funding source than life insurance, typically supporting shorter-tenor bond investments, money-market instruments, and corporate bonds rather than long-duration CGBs.
rics.how_to_use: Company-level property insurance premium data is most relevant for industry-specific analysis (coal sector health, industrial activity insurance penetration) rather than broad bond market signals. In aggregate, property insurance premium growth across the sector tracks economic activity; declining premiums during industrial downturns can reduce NBFI bond demand. Cross-reference with aCNCNJKLPM (Ping An Property) to compare state-affiliated niche insurers with large generalist P&C players.

rics.description: Chinese property insurance companies, premium income, China Ping An Property
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Property Premium Income / Ping An Property
rics.meaning: Monthly premium income of Ping An Property & Casualty Insurance (平安财险), China's largest private property insurer and second-largest overall P&C insurer after PICC. Published by NFRA in monthly P&C statistics. Ping An Property's premium growth is a bellwether for the overall Chinese non-life insurance market, given its scale and diversified product mix (auto insurance dominant, liability, cargo, health add-ons).
rics.how_to_use: Ping An Property's premium income is the best single-company indicator for China P&C sector trends. Use month-on-month growth to gauge auto insurance market health (linked to vehicle sales and renewal rates). From a bond perspective, P&C insurer portfolios are shorter-duration than life; Ping An Property invests heavily in bonds with 1–5 year tenors and in equities. A sustained deceleration in P&C premiums signals reduced demand for short-to-medium-duration corporate credit bonds.

rics.description: Chinese property insurance companies, premium income, Taikang Online
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Property Premium Income / Taikang Online
rics.meaning: Monthly premium income of Taikang Online P&C Insurance (泰康在线财产保险), a digital-channel property insurer affiliated with the Taikang Group. Taikang Online represents the new generation of internet-distributed insurance products in China. Published by NFRA monthly. Online P&C insurers typically have faster growth but smaller scale than traditional P&C players; their investment portfolios are proportionally smaller relative to premiums written.
rics.how_to_use: Use as an indicator of digital insurance channel growth within China's P&C market. Rapid growth at online insurers like Taikang Online signals a structural shift in distribution (away from agents toward apps and platform-based sales), which also affects insurer investment strategy given shorter policy durations and more dynamic premium inflows. For bond market purposes, this series is a minor contributor to total insurance asset demand; the aggregate life insurance series (aCNCNCJSM, aCNCNGIFUM) are more relevant for bond-flow analysis.

rics.description: New foreign insurance company policyholders pay for new investment, AIA
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Foreign Insurer New Investment Payments / AIA
rics.meaning: Monthly new policyholder investment payments (新单投资型保费) at AIA Life Insurance China (友邦人寿), the China subsidiary of AIA Group — the largest foreign life insurer in China. Published by NFRA. AIA China operates through an agency distribution model and focuses on health and protection products, with universal life and investment-linked products generating the investment-type premium captured here. AIA is a bellwether for the foreign insurer segment.
rics.how_to_use: AIA's investment-type premium data tracks the savings insurance demand from China's high-net-worth and upper-middle-class consumers who prefer foreign brand guarantees. Rising AIA investment premiums signals robust demand for insurance savings products — money that flows into Chinese bond and equity markets through AIA's investment portfolio. Compare with domestic counterparts (aCNCNGIFUM) to assess relative market-share trends. AIA's policy-linked investment flows are directionally CNY-positive as they represent onshore reinvestment.

rics.description: New foreign insurance company policyholders pay for new investment, Safe & Sound
rics.subcategory: Insurance — Foreign Insurer New Investment Payments / Safe & Sound
rics.meaning: Monthly new investment policyholder payments at Safe & Sound Insurance (安联人寿 / Allianz China or similar foreign JV entity). Published by NFRA as part of the foreign insurer statistical series. Foreign-invested life insurers in China operate under regulatory caps on foreign ownership (now 100% permitted since 2020) and must invest the majority of their CNY-denominated liabilities in domestic Chinese assets. Foreign insurer premium data collectively tracks an underserved segment that has grown as market access improved.
rics.how_to_use: Foreign insurer premium series provide a unique signal: these companies' investment portfolios must be locally invested, but their parent companies' risk appetite and product design reflect international standards. Rising premiums at foreign insurers signal improving consumer trust in foreign-brand insurance — bullish for the long-term development of China's insurance market depth. For bond markets, aggregate foreign insurer asset flows are modest relative to state-owned insurers, but growing.

rics.description: Margin trading balance amount
rics.meaning: Monthly aggregate of outstanding margin trading balances (融资融券余额) across the Shanghai Stock Exchange and Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Margin finance (融资) allows investors to borrow from brokers to buy securities; securities lending (融券) enables short-selling. The combined balance peaked above CNY 2.3 trillion in 2015 (before the crash), averaged CNY 1.3–1.7 trillion in 2022–24, and is published regularly by the exchanges and SSE/SZSE statistical offices.
rics.how_to_use: Margin trading balance is China's primary retail leverage indicator for equities. A rising balance signals increasing risk appetite and leveraged positioning — often a late-cycle warning sign in bull markets (as in mid-2015 and late-2024 stimulus-driven rallies). A rapid decline signals forced deleveraging. From a bond-market perspective, margin balance moves inversely to risk appetite: de-risking (margin balance decline) typically accompanies capital rotation from equities into bonds, supporting CGB prices. Cross with aCNSHRPRCF (Shanghai Composite) for context.

rics.description: Government Benchmarks, Bid
rics.meaning: Chinese government bond benchmark bid yields across key tenors (1Y, 2Y, 3Y, 5Y, 7Y, 10Y, and possibly 30Y), compiled by Refinitiv from CIBM market-maker quotes. The 10Y CGB bid yield is China's most closely watched long-rate benchmark — analogous to the 10Y UST yield in the US. In 2024, the 10Y CGB hit a historic low near 1.6% as deflation concerns, property-sector weakness, and PBoC easing compressed yields sharply.
rics.how_to_use: The 10Y CGB yield is the key input for China long-rate analysis. Monitor the 10Y CGB-UST spread (aCNGBOND minus 10Y UST) as the primary CNY direction indicator: a narrowing or negative spread drives capital outflows and CNY depreciation pressure. The shape of the CGB yield curve (2Y-10Y slope) signals PBoC policy stance expectations — steepening = easing ahead, flattening = tightening. Use as the risk-free rate for Chinese DCF valuations, LPR reform analysis, and cross-market rate comparisons with aCNLPR5YRR.

rics.description: IFDI, Sustainability, CSR, Disclosed Funds Distributed to Charity, Zakat, and Qard Al Hasan
rics.meaning: Islamic Finance Development Indicator: IFDI, Sustainability, CSR, Disclosed Funds Distributed to Charity, Zakat, and Qard Al Hasan. Reference data on China's Islamic finance footprint (small relative to total finance — concentrated in Ningxia and Xinjiang regions).
rics.how_to_use: Niche reference. China's Islamic-finance market is small but growing. Not a mainstream macroeconomic indicator.

rics.description: Basic medical insurance fund expenditure
rics.subcategory: Healthcare Finance — Basic Medical Insurance Expenditure
rics.meaning: Monthly expenditure of China's basic medical insurance fund (基本医疗保险基金支出), comprising urban employee medical insurance and urban/rural resident medical insurance. Administered by the National Healthcare Security Administration (NHSA) and compiled from provincial statistical reports. Total basic medical insurance fund expenditure exceeded CNY 2.5 trillion annually by the early 2020s. This is a fiscal expenditure series that affects the overall public-sector financing need.
rics.how_to_use: Rapid growth in medical insurance expenditure relative to fund income signals actuarial deficit pressures in China's healthcare system — which may ultimately translate into increased central or local government borrowing to backstop the system. Analysts tracking China's social security fiscal burden should integrate this with pension expenditure and unemployment insurance data to assess total social welfare funding gaps. From a bond-market perspective, larger social welfare deficits expand the LGB or special CGB issuance pipeline.

rics.description: Real estate enterprises, funds actually put in place, Jilin Province
rics.subcategory: Real Estate Finance — Developer Funding / Jilin Province
rics.meaning: Monthly funds actually utilised by real estate enterprises in Jilin Province (吉林省房地产企业到位资金), published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) in its real estate development statistics. This includes domestic loans, self-raised funds, deposits/advances, and mortgage loans. Jilin is a northeastern rust-belt province with historically slow real estate market development; its developer funding data is a regional cross-section of the broader national property financing picture.
rics.how_to_use: Regional developer funding data provides a granular view of real estate financing stress across Chinese provinces. Jilin, as a weaker real estate market, often shows sharper deterioration than national averages in downturns. Track alongside the national bank-loan series (aCNCNOWWPM) and Shanghai mortgage series (aCNCNLGEDM) to build a regional funding-stress matrix. Sustained declines in developer funding — especially domestic loan and mortgage components — in lagging provinces like Jilin signal the last stages of property cycle contraction.

rics.description: Real estate enterprises, funds actually put in place, bank loans
rics.subcategory: Real Estate Finance — Developer Bank Loans (National)
rics.meaning: Monthly bank loans to real estate enterprises nationwide — the bank-loan component of total real estate developer funding (房地产企业到位资金中的国内贷款). Published by the NBS in monthly real estate development statistics. Bank credit to developers (property development loans, land acquisition loans) is the dominant debt funding channel for Chinese property developers; its collapse from 2021 onwards was the primary transmission mechanism of the property-sector debt crisis.
rics.how_to_use: This is the single most important credit-channel indicator for China's property sector. Monitor the year-on-year growth rate: sustained contraction (as during 2022–24) signals banks are tightening developer credit even under official policy easing — a credit-cycle divergence. Improving bank loan flows are a precondition for property market stabilisation. Pair with mortgage data (aCNCNLGEDM, aCNCNZIVVM) and provincial data (aCNCNZJVTM, aCNCNNWZEM) for a full funding-stack decomposition. Affects LGB issuance as local governments must compensate for developer revenue shortfalls.

rics.description: Real estate enterprises, funds actually put in place, domestic loans, Guizhou Province
rics.subcategory: Real Estate Finance — Developer Domestic Loans / Guizhou
rics.meaning: Monthly domestic bank loans to real estate enterprises in Guizhou Province, a southwestern province with one of China's highest LGFV debt burdens. Published by NBS provincial statistical offices. Guizhou's real estate market is a high-risk segment: the province has relied heavily on LGFV-backed property development, and its developer funding data is closely watched during LGFV debt restructuring periods. Financing conditions here are a leading indicator of fiscal stress in the southwest.
rics.how_to_use: Guizhou developer domestic loan data is particularly relevant for LGFV credit analysts because Guizhou was among the first provinces to see explicit LGFV debt restructuring under government guidance in 2023. A sharp decline in developer bank loans in Guizhou alongside rising special refinancing bond issuance (LGB) reflects the active LGFV-to-LGB debt swap dynamic. Pair with national data (aCNCNOWWPM) and Hubei data (aCNCNNWZEM) for regional comparison.

rics.description: Real estate enterprises, funds actually put in place, domestic loans, Hubei Province
rics.subcategory: Real Estate Finance — Developer Domestic Loans / Hubei
rics.meaning: Monthly domestic bank loans to real estate enterprises in Hubei Province (湖北省), a central China province and one of China's larger real estate markets. Hubei includes Wuhan — a Tier-2 city with a large housing market. Published by the NBS in provincial real estate statistics. Hubei's developer funding data captures a mid-tier provincial market less extreme than coastal (Shanghai/Shenzhen) or lagging (Jilin/Guizhou) markets.
rics.how_to_use: Hubei is a useful middle-ground regional indicator between coastal boom markets and lagging provinces. Developer loan trends here track the national median more closely than either extreme. During the post-COVID recovery (2023–24), monitor whether Hubei developer loans are recovering in line with national policy easing; persistent weakness despite PBoC rate cuts would confirm that credit-transmission to the property sector is broken. Cross with aCNCNOWWPM (national) and aCNCNZJVTM (Guizhou) for a geographic spread.

rics.description: Real estate enterprises, funds actually put in place, personal mortgage loans, Heilongjiang Province
rics.subcategory: Real Estate Finance — Developer Mortgage Loans / Heilongjiang
rics.meaning: Monthly personal mortgage loans received by real estate enterprises in Heilongjiang Province (黑龙江省), a northeastern province with one of China's most distressed real estate markets. Mortgage inflows to developers reflect homebuyer advance payments and loan proceeds, which are a primary funding source for construction completion. Heilongjiang's severe housing oversupply and demographic decline make it a stress-test case for mortgage-funding collapse.
rics.how_to_use: Heilongjiang mortgage data is a canary-in-the-coalmine indicator for China's most stressed real estate markets. Persistent declines in mortgage inflows here signal that homebuyer confidence has not recovered despite national policy easing. For bond market analysts, sustained weakness in northeast mortgage markets translates directly into LGFV stress (local government land revenue collapse) and pressure for additional LGB issuance to compensate fiscal shortfalls. Cross with Shanghai mortgage data (aCNCNLGEDM) for a stressed vs resilient market comparison.

rics.description: Real estate enterprises, funds actually put in place, personal mortgage loans, Shanghai Municipality
rics.subcategory: Real Estate Finance — Developer Mortgage Loans / Shanghai
rics.meaning: Monthly personal mortgage loan inflows to real estate enterprises in Shanghai Municipality — the benchmark for China's most liquid and internationally connected real estate market. Shanghai mortgage data reflects premium urban housing demand, typically the first market to recover in a national property cycle. Published by NBS in provincial real estate statistics. Shanghai's 5-year LPR transmission (aCNLPR5YRR) is particularly visible in mortgage affordability here.
rics.how_to_use: Shanghai mortgage data is the most cyclically sensitive signal for the high end of the Chinese property market. Recovery in Shanghai mortgage inflows (year-on-year positive) is typically a leading indicator for broader national property market stabilisation, given Shanghai's trendsetting role. For bond analysts, improving Shanghai mortgage conditions reduce the pressure on LGB special bond issuance (local government needs less fiscal backstop when land sales and housing revenues recover). Pair with aCNLPR5YRR to assess affordability dynamics.

rics.description: Real estate enterprises, funds actually put in place, self-raised funds, Jiangsu Province
rics.subcategory: Real Estate Finance — Developer Self-raised Funds / Jiangsu
rics.meaning: Monthly self-raised funds (自筹资金) of real estate enterprises in Jiangsu Province — including equity capital, internal cash generation, trust financing, and bond proceeds not classified as bank loans. Jiangsu is China's second-largest provincial economy and a major real estate market with cities such as Nanjing, Suzhou, and Wuxi. Self-raised funds are the residual developer funding source when bank loans and mortgage inflows are constrained.
