rics.how_to_use: Self-raised fund data is particularly relevant for tracking shadow financing of real estate developers. When bank loans decline (as post-2021) and mortgage inflows are weak, developers shift to self-raised channels — trust loans, bond issuance, equity injections — which are riskier and costlier. Jiangsu's large and diversified real estate market makes it a representative national indicator. A sustained decline in self-raised funds alongside falling bank loans confirms developers are in a comprehensive funding squeeze, with potential bond default implications.

rics.description: SHANGHAI SE COMPOSITE INDEX - CLOSE
rics.subcategory: Equity Market — Shanghai SE Composite Index (Close)
rics.meaning: Monthly closing level of the Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite Index (上证综合指数, SSE Composite), China's most widely followed domestic equity benchmark. The SSE Composite covers all A-share and B-share stocks listed on the Shanghai exchange (~1,700+ companies). Published daily by the SSE; monthly data in this series reflects the end-of-month close. The index hovered between 2,800 and 3,500 for most of 2022–24 before a stimulus-driven surge above 3,200 in late 2024.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the primary equity/bond risk-rotation indicator. When the SSE Composite sells off sharply, safe-haven flows into CGBs typically follow, compressing CGB yields. The stock-bond correlation in China is broadly negative over multi-year horizons but can be positive during risk-off events driven by systemic concerns. Rising equity markets can drain liquidity from bond funds, putting upward pressure on yields. Cross with aCNMGTBA (margin balance) to detect leverage-driven equity rallies that are more likely to reverse sharply.

rics.description: Listed Companies on National Equities Exchange and Quotations
rics.meaning: Monthly count of companies listed on the National Equities Exchange and Quotations (NEEQ, 全国中小企业股份转让系统 — the 'New Third Board'), China's OTC equity platform for small and medium enterprises. The NEEQ peaked at over 11,000 listed companies in 2017 before regulatory reforms and listings migrated to the Beijing Stock Exchange (BSE, launched 2021). As of 2024, the NEEQ listed company count is several thousand. Published monthly by NEEQ and Cninfo.
rics.how_to_use: Use as an indicator of SME access to formal equity capital markets. A declining listed-company count reflects either voluntary de-listings (companies migrating to BSE or other exchanges) or involuntary exits (financial difficulties). For bond market analysis, SME capital access from NEEQ is a substitute/complement to SME bond markets (SME collective notes, aCNBCSCNNA); when equity issuance conditions deteriorate for SMEs, bond funding demand rises. Track NEEQ company count alongside aCNNEFREQA (funds raised) for a complete equity funding picture.

rics.description: Number of Times NEEQ Listed Companies Issued Shares, Incl Additional Shares
rics.subcategory: Equity Market — NEEQ Share Issuance Frequency
rics.meaning: Monthly count of the number of times NEEQ-listed companies issued shares (including additional share issuances), as reported by NEEQ and Cninfo. This measures the frequency of equity capital-raising transactions on the New Third Board platform, spanning IPO initial listings, secondary offerings, private placements, and rights issues. High issuance frequency indicates active use of the NEEQ as a capital-raising vehicle by SMEs.
rics.how_to_use: A rising issuance frequency alongside growing funds raised (aCNNEFREQA) confirms robust NEEQ primary market activity — positive for SME financing conditions. Declining frequency signals that SMEs are finding NEEQ fundraising less attractive (often due to low secondary market liquidity or regulatory burden). For bond analysts, NEEQ equity issuance activity is a substitute for SME bond issuance; when NEEQ activity falls, monitor aCNBCSCNNA (SME collective notes) for compensating debt-market issuance.

rics.description: Total Funds Raised on National Equities Exchange and Quotations
rics.subcategory: Equity Market — NEEQ Total Funds Raised
rics.meaning: Monthly total funds raised through equity issuance on the National Equities Exchange and Quotations (NEEQ). This captures the aggregate proceeds from all share issuances by NEEQ-listed SMEs including IPOs, private placements, and rights issues. NEEQ annual fundraising peaked at over CNY 200 billion before 2018 regulatory reforms; post-reform it stabilised at lower levels as the BSE was established as a more regulated tier above NEEQ. Published by NEEQ and Cninfo.
rics.how_to_use: NEEQ funds raised is an SME equity market vitality indicator. Compare year-on-year to assess SME capital market conditions. For macro analysts, aggregate NEEQ equity issuance — though relatively small — represents a formal private equity channel complementary to bank loans and bond markets. Rising NEEQ fundraising alongside weak SME loan growth suggests a channel-switching dynamic. From a bond perspective, strong SME equity fundraising reduces SME demand for credit bonds, easing supply pressure in aCNBCSCNNA and commercial paper (aCNBCCMPCA).

rics.description: Total Issued Shares on National Equities Exchange and Quotations, Annual, National Equities Exchange and Quotations(NEEQ) & Cninfo, China
rics.subcategory: Equity Market — NEEQ Total Issued Shares (Annual)
rics.meaning: Annual total number of shares issued by NEEQ-listed companies, as reported by NEEQ and Cninfo. This annual series (frequency P1Y) captures the cumulative share count issued during each calendar year across all NEEQ participants including new listings and additional issuances. The annual frequency means this series provides a full-year stock-taking of equity market activity at the SME level.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the annual baseline for computing per-company average share issuance on the NEEQ. When combined with aCNNEFREQA (CNY raised), divide total funds raised by total shares issued to derive an implied average issuance price — a rough equity valuation indicator for NEEQ SMEs. For trend analysis, the annual series is preferable when monthly volatility obscures structural patterns. A multi-year decline in annual NEEQ shares issued confirms structural disengagement from the platform.

rics.description: Total Issued Shares on National Equities Exchange and Quotations, Monthly, National Equities Exchange and Quotations(NEEQ) & Cninfo, China
rics.subcategory: Equity Market — NEEQ Total Issued Shares (Monthly)
rics.meaning: Monthly total number of shares issued by NEEQ-listed companies, the higher-frequency counterpart to the annual series aCNNEIVEP. Published monthly by NEEQ and Cninfo. Monthly share issuance data captures seasonal and cyclical patterns in SME equity fundraising — typically higher in Q4 (year-end planning), lower during regulatory review windows, and correlated with broader equity market conditions on the SSE/SZSE.
rics.how_to_use: The monthly series enables real-time tracking of NEEQ primary market momentum. Large month-on-month swings often reflect regulatory windows (opening/closing of specific listing types) rather than pure market dynamics. Use rolling 3-month or 12-month averages to identify underlying trends. Combined with aCNNEFREQA (CNY raised monthly), this derives implied monthly average issue prices. Relevant for policy analysts monitoring the effectiveness of capital market reforms aimed at SME equity financing.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Credit Cooperatives
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS holdings by rural and urban credit cooperatives. Credit cooperatives are small regional lenders that participate in the interbank ABS market primarily as senior-tranche investors seeking modest yield premium over bank deposits. Their ABS holdings are typically small relative to state-owned commercial banks but are informative about risk appetite at the smaller-institution tier of China's banking system.
rics.how_to_use: Track as a gauge of ABS demand breadth — rising credit cooperative ABS holdings indicate the investor base is widening beyond large banks to smaller institutions, typically a positive sign for ABS market development. Combine with aCNHCABCBA (state-owned commercial bank holdings) and aCNHCABTOA (total) to compute the large-bank vs small-institution ABS holding ratio. A high concentration of ABS in large banks and falling credit cooperative holdings signals deteriorating small-institution confidence in ABS credit quality.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Depository Financial Institutions
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — Depository Financial Institutions
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS holdings by all depository financial institutions as a group (banks and deposit-taking cooperatives). This broad category aggregates ABS held by state banks, joint-stock banks, city commercial banks, rural commercial banks, credit cooperatives, and foreign banks. It is the dominant demand category for Chinese interbank ABS, as deposit-funded institutions are the natural buyer for senior-tranche securitised assets.
rics.how_to_use: Depository institution ABS holdings represent the core demand base for China's securitisation market. Use as the primary demand indicator: sustained growth confirms banks are actively using ABS as a yield-enhancing alternative to bonds and loans. Compare with non-depository holders (insurance: aCNHCABIIA, funds: aCNHCABFIA) to assess market broadening. During regulatory tightening on bank balance sheets, rising ABS holdings by depositories can signal regulatory arbitrage — moving assets off-balance-sheet while retaining economic exposure.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Foreign Banks
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on interbank credit ABS held by foreign bank branches and subsidiaries operating in China. Foreign banks' ABS holdings in China are small — foreign bank participation in the ABS market is limited by their smaller balance sheets and more conservative risk frameworks. However, their presence signals improving transparency and credit quality in Chinese ABS, as foreign institutions apply rigorous due diligence.
rics.how_to_use: Foreign bank ABS holdings are a quality-signal indicator: if foreign banks are buying, it implies the ABS meets international underwriting standards. Rising foreign bank ABS holdings signal improving Chinese securitisation market credibility. For analysts tracking cross-border investment in Chinese structured products, this series provides granularity on the foreign-bank subset of aCNHCABIVA (foreign investor aggregate). Compare with aCNHCABIVA for the full foreign participation picture.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Foreign Investor
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House aggregate of credit ABS held by all foreign investors — combining foreign bank branches and offshore institutional investors accessing China's interbank ABS via Bond Connect or CIBM Direct. Total foreign ABS holdings are modest (typically below CNY 100 billion) given the complexity of Chinese ABS legal structures and the limited secondary-market liquidity, but have grown as China expanded Bond Connect eligible instruments to include ABS.
rics.how_to_use: Track as the broadest measure of foreign participation in China's ABS market. Compare month-on-month changes with aCNHSFIANA (ChinaBond-tracked foreign ABS holdings) as a cross-check — the two registries together cover the full foreign ABS position. A sustained increase in foreign ABS holdings signals that China's structured credit market is internationalising. For credit-risk analysts, foreign investor ABS demand is a useful price-quality signal: if foreign holdings rise while domestic investors are flat, implied credit quality improvements are being recognised internationally.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Funds Companies
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS holdings by fund management companies (公募基金). Fund companies managing bond mutual funds, money market funds, and ABS-specific funds participate in the interbank ABS market as investors in senior and mezzanine tranches. Their ABS holdings are sensitive to redemption pressure from retail investors — a sudden outflow from bond funds can force ABS sales, widening spreads.
rics.how_to_use: Fund company ABS holdings are a price-volatility indicator for the ABS market. Unlike buy-and-hold bank investors, fund managers are forced to sell when facing redemptions — making fund holdings the more volatile portion of ABS demand. Monitor aCNHCABFCA alongside aCNHCABFIA (fund institutions, including social security and pension funds) to distinguish discretionary from constrained sellers. A spike in redemption-driven ABS selling by fund companies is a precursor to broader credit spread widening.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Funds Institutions
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on ABS holdings by fund institutions — including social security funds, pension funds, enterprise annuity funds, and insurance asset management companies acting as fund trustees. These institutional fund managers typically have longer investment horizons than retail-facing fund companies (aCNHCABFCA), making them more stable holders of ABS across credit cycles.
rics.how_to_use: Fund institution ABS holdings are a structural demand indicator. Social security and pension fund ABS demand is driven by actuarial return requirements rather than market timing — rising holdings signal a mandate extension to structured credit. When MOHRSS (Ministry of Human Resources) allows social security fund ABS investments, this series captures the follow-through. Cross with aCNHCABFCA (public fund companies) to distinguish long-term from potentially forced sellers in the ABS investor base.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Insurance financial institutions
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by insurance companies and insurance asset management entities. Insurance ABS holdings reflect the sector's search for yield above CGB rates while maintaining high credit quality in senior tranches. Life insurers are particularly important ABS investors given their need for duration-matching and regulatory push toward diverse fixed-income assets under CBIRC's C-ROSS solvency framework.
rics.how_to_use: Insurance ABS demand is structurally growing as China's insurance sector assets under management expand with premium inflows. Rising insurance institution ABS holdings signal growing acceptance of securitised credit as a core portfolio asset class alongside government bonds. Monitor alongside aCNHSIILNA (insurance LGB holdings) and aCNCNGIFUM (insurance premium income) to link premium inflows to the diversification of investment across bonds, ABS, and other fixed income. ABS yields typically 30–80 bps above comparable-duration CGB — an attractive spread for yield-hungry insurers.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Joint-Stock Commercial Banks,
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — Joint-stock Commercial Banks
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS holdings by joint-stock commercial banks (股份制商业银行) — the tier of banks below the Big Six state-owned banks, including China Merchants Bank, CITIC Bank, Minsheng Bank, Guangfa Bank, Industrial Bank, and others. Joint-stock banks are active ABS investors seeking yield enhancement and, as active originators themselves, also hold subordinated tranches of their own securitisations.
rics.how_to_use: Joint-stock bank ABS demand is closely tied to their loan-growth and capital strategies. When joint-stock banks are actively originating (high credit growth), they also tend to invest in peer ABS to recycle capital. Declining joint-stock bank ABS holdings often precede credit stress — these banks are usually quicker than state banks to de-risk when credit quality deteriorates. Compare with aCNHCABCBA (state-owned commercial banks) to track the state vs private bank risk-appetite divergence in structured credit.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Nominee Account (Domestic)
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held in domestic nominee accounts (名义持有人账户). Nominee accounts are custodial structures used by investment managers holding ABS on behalf of multiple beneficial owners — primarily fund companies managing ABS-invested products and wealth management subsidiaries of banks. The nominee account structure aggregates holdings that would otherwise be fragmented across individual client accounts.
rics.how_to_use: Nominee account ABS holdings capture the indirect institutional demand for ABS routed through asset managers and bank wealth management (WMP) vehicles. Rising nominee account ABS holdings signal growing retail/HNWI indirect exposure to structured credit through WMPs — an important channel for assessing shadow banking leverage in ABS. If nominee account holdings grow rapidly while direct bank holdings are flat, it suggests ABS demand is being channelled through off-balance-sheet or lightly regulated structures. Monitor alongside aCNHCABFCA for the full intermediated demand picture.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Non-financial Institutions
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by non-financial corporations and institutions — including large state-owned enterprises, industrial groups, and treasury functions of corporate entities that invest surplus cash in short-to-medium-duration ABS for yield enhancement. Non-financial institution ABS investment is a niche but growing channel as corporate treasury management in China becomes more sophisticated.
rics.how_to_use: Non-financial institution ABS holdings are a corporate liquidity indicator. Rising holdings suggest large corporates have surplus cash available for investment — a positive indicator for corporate health and capital markets depth. Declining holdings can signal corporates are liquidating investment portfolios to fund operations or capital expenditures, which may coincide with economic stress. Cross with aCNHCABTOA to compute the non-financial corporate share of total ABS demand — typically small (sub-5%) but with cyclical variation.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Other Depository Financial Institutions
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — Other Depository Financial Institutions
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by other depository financial institutions not captured in standard commercial bank categories — including postal savings institutions, rural credit cooperatives not separately identified, and specialized depository entities. This residual depository category provides additional granularity within the broader depository financial institution group (aCNHCABDFA).
rics.how_to_use: This residual depository ABS series is most useful as a consistency check for the full investor-type breakdown. If aCNHCABDFA grows faster than the sum of its named subcategories plus aCNHCABIFA, reclassification may have occurred. For substantive analysis, aggregate with the named commercial bank categories. Growth here may also indicate expansion of postal savings bank participation in ABS, given PSBC's large deposit base and growing capital market investment mandate.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Other financial institutions
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — Other Financial Institutions
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by other financial institutions not classified into specific categories — including trust companies, financial leasing companies, consumer finance companies, auto finance companies, and other licensed NBFIs. These institutions are both originators of ABS collateral (e.g., auto finance companies originating auto-loan ABS) and investors in peer ABS products.
rics.how_to_use: Monitor as an indicator of intra-sector recycling within China's NBFI ecosystem. When auto finance companies and consumer finance firms hold significant ABS (often their own or peers'), it signals active use of securitisation for balance-sheet management. Rising 'other financial institution' ABS holdings during periods of tighter bank lending signals active substitution — NBFIs expanding through securitisation when banks are constrained. Pair with aCNBINFICP (NBFI bond issuance) for a full NBFI capital market activity picture.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Others
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House residual category for credit ABS holdings not classified into the named investor groups. This 'Others' bucket includes government entities, quasi-government funds, and individual investors (where permitted). In practice, this is typically a small balancing category that ensures the sum of all named investor-type series equals aCNHCABTOA (total ABS holdings).
rics.how_to_use: Use as a cross-check to verify that the investor-type breakdown series for ABS sum correctly to the total (aCNHCABTOA). If 'Others' is persistently large, it may signal incomplete categorisation or growing participation by non-traditional ABS investors. For systematic data quality monitoring in the terminal, flag unusual spikes in this residual category for potential reclassification. Substantive analysis should focus on the named investor-type series.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Policy Banks
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by China's three policy banks (CDB, ADBC, Eximbank). Policy bank ABS holdings are modest — these institutions are primarily bond issuers rather than ABS investors — but their participation signals official-sector endorsement of the securitisation market. CDB in particular may hold ABS related to infrastructure financing structures or rural credit ABS backed by ADBC-originated loans.
rics.how_to_use: Policy bank ABS holdings are a structural integrity signal for China's ABS market. Their presence as investors (even in small amounts) provides reputational support and helps establish market standards. From an analytical perspective, this series is small enough that the level matters less than directional changes: policy banks buying more ABS may signal a government policy push to develop the securitisation market for specific sectors (rural credit, green assets). Pair with aCNHCABCBA (state-owned commercial bank holdings) for the full official-sector ABS demand picture.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Rural Commercial Banks and Coorperative Banks
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — Rural Commercial Banks and Cooperative Banks
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by rural commercial banks and rural cooperative banks — institutions that serve agricultural and small-town markets, typically with concentrated loan books. These banks participate in the ABS market to diversify their asset base beyond local loans and deposits, investing primarily in senior tranches of nationally diversified ABS pools. Their ABS holdings reflect rural financial system participation in capital markets.
rics.how_to_use: Rural commercial bank ABS demand is a market-breadth indicator for China's securitisation market. Rising rural bank ABS holdings signal that the investor base is expanding beyond the urban banking system — improving geographic diversification of ABS demand. For credit analysts, rural banks as ABS investors represent a higher-risk, yield-sensitive segment: they tend to exit ABS positions earlier than state banks during stress periods. Track alongside aCNHCABCCA (credit cooperatives) for the full rural financial institution ABS demand picture.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Securities Companies
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by securities companies (broker-dealers). Securities firms participate in the ABS market as underwriters, market makers, and proprietary investors. Their proprietary ABS holdings tend to be in mezzanine and subordinated tranches — reflecting higher yield targets and shorter holding periods than banks or insurers. Regulatory capital rules for broker ABS holdings differ from banking rules.
rics.how_to_use: Securities company ABS holdings are a risk-appetite indicator for China's broker-dealer community. Rapid build-up of broker ABS holdings is a late-cycle risk signal — brokers taking on structured credit exposure to boost proprietary returns. A sharp decline in broker ABS positions can precede market-wide spread widening as dealers simultaneously reduce exposure. Cross with aCNHSSCANA (ChinaBond-tracked securities company ABS holdings from the other registry) to build the full broker ABS picture across both clearing systems.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - State-owned Commercial Banks
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — State-owned Commercial Banks
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by China's Big Six state-owned commercial banks (ICBC, CCB, ABC, BOC, BoCom, and PSBC). State-owned commercial banks are the dominant force in China's ABS investor base, holding the majority of senior ABS tranches. Their ABS investment is partly driven by capital management (securitising their own loans frees capital; investing in diversified ABS allocates capital at attractive risk-adjusted returns).
rics.how_to_use: State-owned bank ABS holdings are the anchor of China's ABS demand base. Large month-on-month changes here reflect not just market conditions but also regulatory guidance — when CBIRC requires state banks to increase capital buffers, they may reduce ABS holdings to reduce risk-weighted assets. Conversely, PBoC-guided credit expansion often correlates with rising ABS holdings. Use aCNHCABCBA as the primary demand indicator; if state bank ABS demand is weak, the entire primary ABS market suffers regardless of smaller investors' activity.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Total
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House aggregate of total credit ABS holdings across all investor categories — the sum of holdings by state-owned banks, joint-stock banks, city commercial banks, rural banks, credit cooperatives, securities companies, fund companies, insurance institutions, foreign investors, non-financial institutions, and others. This is the primary total-market ABS demand series from the Shanghai Clearing House registry.
rics.how_to_use: The central reference series for China's interbank ABS market size from the Shanghai Clearing House perspective. Compare with aCNHSTCANA (ChinaBond-tracked ABS holdings) to verify consistency between the two registries and arrive at a combined total. Month-on-month changes equal net ABS issuance minus redemptions (from the demand side). Use as the denominator for all investor-share calculations. Year-on-year growth rate against total bond market growth (aCNOVBDONA) shows whether ABS is gaining market share.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Urban Commercial Banks
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — Urban Commercial Banks
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by urban commercial banks (城市商业银行) — the tier of city-level banks including Bank of Beijing, Bank of Shanghai, Bank of Jiangsu, and hundreds of smaller city banks. Urban commercial banks are important ABS investors seeking diversification away from concentrated local loan books; their ABS demand is sensitive to local economic conditions and regulatory capital constraints.
rics.how_to_use: Urban commercial bank ABS holdings capture a segment of the banking sector under particular stress during China's property downturn — many city banks have concentrated exposures to local real estate and LGFVs. When urban commercial banks are reducing ABS holdings, it often signals deteriorating capital positions requiring risk-weighted asset reduction. Compare with aCNHCABJCA (joint-stock banks) and aCNHCABCBA (state-owned banks) to assess the size-vs-risk divergence in ABS demand across bank tiers.

rics.description: Asset-backed Securities - Village and Small Town Banks
rics.subcategory: ABS Holding Structure — Village and Small Town Banks
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on credit ABS held by village banks (村镇银行) and other small-town financial institutions. Village banks are the smallest formally licensed banking institutions in China — typically with very limited capital and concentrated local lending. Their ABS holdings are minimal but represent the most geographically peripheral tier of China's banking system accessing capital markets.
rics.how_to_use: Village bank ABS holdings are primarily a market-breadth and financial inclusion indicator. A positive and growing balance signals that even the smallest rural lenders have access to interbank capital market instruments — a financial development milestone. In credit stress scenarios, village banks are typically the first to exit ABS positions and the last to re-enter. For risk-monitoring purposes, compare this series against aCNHCABRCA (rural commercial banks) to track the rural banking system's aggregate ABS exposure.

rics.description: Bonds Depository: Commercial Papers
rics.meaning: Monthly outstanding stock of commercial papers (CP, 商业票据/短期融资券) registered at Shanghai Clearing House. CP in China's NAFMII-regulated interbank market includes short-term commercial paper (SCP, tenors up to 9 months) and standard commercial paper (CP, up to 1 year) issued by large corporates for short-term working capital funding. Shanghai Clearing House is the primary registry for NAFMII-supervised CP instruments. Total CP outstanding is typically CNY 4–6 trillion.
rics.how_to_use: Commercial paper outstanding is a high-frequency indicator of corporate short-term funding conditions. Rising CP stock signals that corporates are actively drawing on short-term bond markets for working capital — positive for economic activity when driven by demand-side factors. Declining CP stock can indicate: (1) corporates have sufficient internal cash (positive), (2) investors are demanding higher rates making CP unattractive, or (3) issuer credit quality concerns limiting access. Cross with aCNIPCMPCA (interest paid on CP) to gauge average financing cost for corporate short-term borrowing.

rics.description: Bonds Depository: Financial Bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly outstanding stock of financial bonds registered at Shanghai Clearing House. Financial bonds here include bank-issued instruments cleared at Shanghai CH (supplementing the ChinaBond registry for bank bonds), as well as financial bonds issued by securities companies, consumer finance entities, and other NAFMII-supervised financial institutions. Shanghai Clearing House registers a different subset of financial bonds than ChinaBond, providing complementary coverage.
rics.how_to_use: This series from Shanghai Clearing House complements aCNBDCMBNA (ChinaBond commercial bank bonds) and aCNBDNFBNA (ChinaBond non-bank financial bonds). Together they provide a more complete picture of total financial sector bond outstanding. Monitor month-on-month growth for signs of wholesale funding expansion in the financial sector. Rising Shanghai CH financial bond outstanding while ChinaBond bank bond growth is stable indicates growth in the NAFMII/short-duration segment of financial bond issuance.

rics.description: Bonds Depository: Medium-term Notes
rics.meaning: Monthly outstanding stock of Medium-Term Notes (MTN, 中期票据) registered at Shanghai Clearing House (上海清算所). MTNs are NAFMII-supervised corporate bonds with tenors of 1–10 years (typically 3Y or 5Y), issued by large and medium-sized corporations for general funding. The MTN market is one of China's largest corporate bond segments with outstanding exceeding CNY 13–15 trillion. Shanghai Clearing House is the primary registrar for all NAFMII-supervised MTNs.
rics.how_to_use: MTN outstanding is the most important series for China's corporate credit bond supply-demand tracking. Rising MTN stock reflects active corporate use of the capital markets for medium-term funding — substituting for bank loans or bridge financing. Month-on-month changes combined with aCNBIMTNCA (new MTN issuance) and aCNIPCCBNA (interest paid on corporate credit bonds) provide a complete MTN flow-cost-stock accounting. MTN spreads over policy bank bonds are the benchmark for Chinese investment-grade corporate credit spreads.

rics.description: Bonds Depository: SME Collective Notes
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository — SME Collective Notes (Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly outstanding stock of SME Collective Notes (中小企业集合票据) registered at Shanghai Clearing House. SME Collective Notes are a NAFMII-created instrument that pools 2–10 SMEs into a single bond issuance, allowing smaller firms below the individual MTN issuance threshold to access the interbank bond market. Tenors are typically 3–5 years. The market is relatively small (tens of billions CNY outstanding) but strategically important for SME financing policy.
rics.how_to_use: SME Collective Note outstanding is a policy-efficacy indicator for China's SME capital market access initiatives. Rising outstanding signals policy success in channelling bond market financing to smaller enterprises; stagnation suggests SMEs remain reliant on bank loans or informal financing. From a bond-market perspective, SME collective notes carry higher credit risk than large-corporate MTNs, offering a spread premium. Monitor alongside aCNNEFREQA (NEEQ equity fundraising) to assess the equity-vs-debt mix of SME capital formation.

rics.description: Bonds Depository: Short-term Securities Companies Financing Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Depository — Short-term Securities Co. Financing Bonds (Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly outstanding stock of short-term securities company financing bonds (证券公司短期融资券) registered at Shanghai Clearing House. These are wholesale short-term funding instruments issued by broker-dealers for working capital, repo margin, and proprietary trading finance, with maturities typically under 1 year. The securities company CP market is sensitive to broker-dealer funding conditions and regulatory leverage limits.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a real-time proxy for broker-dealer leverage and funding stress. Rising outstanding signals brokers are borrowing heavily via capital markets — often coinciding with market-making expansion, proprietary bond positions, or derivatives margining needs. A sudden decline or issuance failure in this segment (failed CP auction at a broker) is an early warning of broker funding stress, which can rapidly propagate to the CIBM via repo market contagion. Cross with aCNBINFICP (new issuance) and aCNBSNFCNA (CIBM settlement) for a full broker funding-market picture.

rics.description: Bonds Interest Paid: Asset-backed Securities
rics.meaning: Monthly coupon interest payments on credit asset-backed securities, as recorded by Shanghai Clearing House. ABS interest payments reflect the aggregate cash flows distributed by SPV trustees to ABS holders across all outstanding tranches. The series measures the current-period income flow to ABS investors — critical for ABS fund cashflow modelling and for tracking the effective cost of securitised funding for originators.
rics.how_to_use: Monthly ABS interest payments provide the income side of ABS return analysis. Divide by aCNHCABTOA (total ABS outstanding) to compute an implied average coupon yield on the ABS market. Rising average coupon (rising interest paid relative to outstanding) signals either rising rates at issuance or a shift toward higher-coupon ABS structures. For bank originators, compare total ABS interest outflows with the cost of wholesale funding alternatives (NCD rates, financial bond coupons) to assess securitisation cost-effectiveness.

rics.description: Bonds Interest Paid: Commercial Papers
rics.subcategory: Bond Interest Paid — Commercial Papers (Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly interest paid on commercial papers (CP and SCP) registered at Shanghai Clearing House — representing the aggregate coupon and discount interest distributed to CP holders from corporate issuers. Since CP is typically issued at a discount to par, 'interest paid' reflects the discount amortisation plus any explicit coupon. Monthly CP interest payments are sensitive to money-market rates, as CP pricing is anchored to SHIBOR and repo rates.
rics.how_to_use: Divide by aCNBCCMPCA (outstanding CP stock) to derive an implied average CP yield — a high-frequency indicator of corporate short-term borrowing costs. When implied CP yields diverge from SHIBOR rates, it signals either credit spread widening for corporate issuers (rising CP yields vs stable SHIBOR) or unusual technical conditions. Compare corporate CP financing costs (aCNIPCMPCA / aCNBCCMPCA) with aCNLPR1YRR to assess whether the bond market offers cheaper short-term funding than bank loans.

rics.description: Bonds Interest Paid: Corporate Credit Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Interest Paid — Corporate Credit Bonds (CNY, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly coupon interest paid on corporate credit bonds registered at Shanghai Clearing House, in CNY current-price terms. Corporate credit bonds under NAFMII supervision include MTNs, commercial papers, SME collective notes, non-financial institution bonds, and super-short-term commercial paper (SCP). This series captures the total coupon cash flows distributed to investors monthly, providing a direct measure of corporate bond financing costs at the aggregate level.
rics.how_to_use: Combine with aCNBCMTNCA and aCNBCCMPCA (outstanding) to compute an implied weighted-average corporate bond yield. Track month-on-month changes: rising interest payments relative to stable outstanding signal higher coupon rates at issuance (rate environment change) or maturity extension (longer duration, higher absolute coupon). This series is useful for computing the aggregate corporate bond interest burden — relevant for default-risk and debt-sustainability analysis. Compare with the CNY volume counterpart aCNIPCCBNA.

rics.description: Bonds Interest Paid: Corporate Credit Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Interest Paid — Corporate Credit Bonds (volume, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly coupon interest paid on corporate credit bonds in notional/face-value volume terms — the notional counterpart to aCNIPCCBCA (current-price CNY). Corporate credit bonds here cover the full NAFMII-supervised spectrum: MTNs, CP, SCP, SME collective notes, and NBFI bonds. The notional vs current-price distinction matters when bonds trade at significant premium or discount to par. Published by Shanghai Clearing House monthly.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNIPCCBCA to cross-check whether market-price movements are materially affecting the interest payment calculation. In China's 2024 bond rally (prices significantly above par), current-price interest (aCNIPCCBCA) would modestly exceed notional-basis interest (aCNIPCCBNA). For corporate financing cost analysis, the notional basis is more appropriate for comparing against face-value debt outstanding. Pair with aCNBCMTNCA and aCNBCCMPCA (outstanding) for a full interest-coverage ratio calculation.

rics.description: Bonds Interest Paid: Panda bonds
rics.meaning: Monthly coupon interest paid on panda bonds (熊猫债) — CNY-denominated bonds issued by non-Chinese entities (sovereign issuers, multilateral development banks, foreign corporations, and foreign financial institutions) in China's onshore bond market, registered primarily at Shanghai Clearing House. Issuers have included sovereigns from Belt and Road countries, the World Bank, ADB, and foreign corporates. Panda bond outstanding has grown to CNY 300–500 billion by the mid-2020s as interest in accessing CNY funding has grown.
rics.how_to_use: Panda bond interest payments divided by aCNBIPDBNA (panda bond outstanding from issuance cumulation) give an implied panda bond average yield — the CNY borrowing rate for foreign issuers. Monitoring this spread versus comparable CGB yields reveals the 'panda premium' (or discount) paid by foreign issuers for CNY funding. Rising panda bond interest payments signal both market growth and potentially rising CNY rates. For CNY internationalisation analysts, growing panda interest flows demonstrate deepening two-way capital market integration.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Asset-backed Securities, Current Prices, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.meaning: Monthly gross issuance of credit asset-backed securities in CNY terms, as reported by Shanghai Clearing House. This captures all new interbank ABS transactions registered at Shanghai CH — auto-loan ABS, corporate-loan CLOs, credit-card ABS, and RMBS — at face value in current-price CNY. Monthly ABS issuance has grown from near-zero pre-2012 to CNY 200–500 billion per month at peak levels, reflecting banks' ongoing use of securitisation for capital and balance-sheet management.
rics.how_to_use: Track as the primary indicator of primary ABS market activity. Month-on-month spikes often reflect large state bank securitisation mandates or regulatory-encouraged ABS windows. Combine with aCNBIABSNP (volume count) to compute average ABS deal size — a proxy for market standardisation. Use rolling 12-month total versus aCNBDCASNA (outstanding stock) to compute the net ABS flow rate. Rising issuance during low-yield environments signals banks are actively securitising to free up capital for new lending rather than for yield arbitrage.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Asset-backed Securities, Volume, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.units: Number of tranches or CNY billion (notional)
rics.meaning: Monthly ABS issuance in volume terms (notional face value or tranche count) from Shanghai Clearing House — the volume counterpart to aCNBIABSNA (current prices). The distinction between the 'NA' (current price) and 'NP' (volume/notional) variants allows for assessment of issuance price versus par value, and the 'NP' series may also track transaction count. Published simultaneously with aCNBIABSNA as part of Shanghai Clearing House monthly issuance statistics.
rics.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNBIABSNA to derive average ABS issue pricing relative to par. In China's 2024 bond rally, ABS issued above par would show aCNBIABSNA > aCNBIABSNP. If the series tracks transaction count, divide aCNBIABSNA (CNY value) by aCNBIABSNP (count) to get average deal size. Large deal sizes indicate institutional-scale securitisations (state bank CLOs); small average sizes indicate retail or SME-focused ABS programmes. Pair with aCNHCABTOA (investor holdings) to close the issuance-holdings accounting loop.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Corporate Credit Bonds, Current Prices, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Corporate Credit Bonds (CNY, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly gross issuance of corporate credit bonds in CNY current-price terms, registered at Shanghai Clearing House. This covers NAFMII-supervised corporate credit instruments including MTNs, commercial papers, SCP, SME collective notes, and other corporate bond formats under PBOC/NAFMII regulatory supervision. Monthly corporate credit bond issuance regularly reaches CNY 1–3 trillion, making this one of the most important primary market series in China's bond ecosystem.
rics.how_to_use: Monthly corporate credit bond issuance is a direct measure of corporate funding demand and market conditions. High issuance relative to recent history signals: (1) refinancing waves (redemption pressure driving roll-over), (2) opportunistic funding ahead of expected rate rises, or (3) fiscal/stimulus-driven capex funding. Combine with aCNBRTOTNA (total redemptions) to compute net corporate credit bond issuance. The spread of MTN issuance yields over policy bank bonds is the investment-grade corporate credit benchmark — widening spreads deter issuance, narrowing spreads encourage it.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Corporate Credit Bonds, Volume, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Corporate Credit Bonds (volume, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly corporate credit bond issuance in volume/notional terms from Shanghai Clearing House, the volume counterpart to aCNBICCBNA. As with other NP/CP series pairs, this provides the notional-value or transaction-count perspective alongside the current-price CNY total. Differences between the two series reflect bond issuance premium/discount dynamics. Published simultaneously with aCNBICCBNA.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a cross-check against aCNBICCBNA to assess whether corporate bonds are being issued at premium or discount to par (indicating market rate vs coupon divergence). If transaction count is included, compute average corporate credit deal size: concentration in large deals indicates mega-SOE issuance; smaller average deals signal broadening market access for mid-sized corporates. Combine with aCNBCMTNCA (outstanding MTN stock) and aCNBCCMPCA (CP outstanding) for the full primary-to-secondary stock reconciliation.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Green Notes, Current Prices, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Green Notes (CNY, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly gross issuance of green notes (绿色债券/绿色票据) in CNY terms, registered at Shanghai Clearing House. China is the world's second-largest green bond market (after the EU), with annual green bond issuance exceeding CNY 1 trillion by the early 2020s. Green notes under NAFMII supervision include green MTNs, green commercial papers, and green asset-backed notes, with proceeds earmarked for renewable energy, clean transportation, energy efficiency, and green infrastructure. Published monthly by Shanghai Clearing House.
rics.how_to_use: Track as the primary indicator of green finance market activity in China's corporate bond sector. Month-on-month growth reveals seasonal patterns (Q2 and Q4 typically peak) and response to regulatory green finance incentives. Compare aCNBIGRNNA (current price) with aCNBIGRNNP (notional) to check issuance pricing; compare with the volume-variant aCNBIGRNCA and aCNBIGRNCP for the full four-series cross-check. Use year-on-year growth relative to total corporate credit bond issuance (aCNBICCBNA) to compute the green share — a key sustainable-finance policy indicator.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Green Notes, Current Prices, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Green Notes (CNY current price, variant)
rics.meaning: A current-price CNY variant of monthly green note issuance data from Shanghai Clearing House — companion to aCNBIGRNNA. The presence of two current-price CNY green note issuance series ('NA' and 'CA') may reflect different sub-classifications (e.g., exchange-listed vs interbank green notes, or carbon-neutral bonds vs standard green bonds) or the same data published via different reporting pathways. Both series track NAFMII-supervised green note primary market activity.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-reference aCNBIGRNCA against aCNBIGRNNA to identify whether these series capture overlapping or distinct green note populations. If values diverge, the 'CA' series may cover exchange-listed green bonds while 'NA' covers interbank. For comprehensive green bond issuance tracking, use both alongside the volume variants (aCNBIGRNCP and aCNBIGRNNP). China's green bond taxonomy (updated in 2021 to align with international standards) means issuance definitions have evolved — monitor for data discontinuities around taxonomy update dates.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Green Notes, Volume, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Green Notes (volume, variant 1, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly green note issuance in volume/notional terms from Shanghai Clearing House — one of two volume-series variants for green note issuance (the other being aCNBIGRNNP). Volume data complements the current-price series (aCNBIGRNCA, aCNBIGRNNA) by enabling pricing-at-issuance analysis and transaction-count tracking. The 'CP' suffix suggests a current-price basis or count variant from a specific data source.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside the other three green note issuance series (aCNBIGRNNA, aCNBIGRNCA, aCNBIGRNNP) for a complete four-way cross-check of green bond primary market data. Consistent values across CNY price and volume variants confirm data quality; divergences may indicate premium/discount issuance or sub-market definitional differences. For green finance policy tracking, the ratio of green note issuance to total corporate credit bond issuance (aCNBICCBNA) is the key sustainability-transition metric.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Green Notes, Volume, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Green Notes (volume, variant 2, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly green note issuance in volume/notional terms — the second of two volume-series variants for green notes from Shanghai Clearing House. This 'NP' suffix series (notional-price or volume) pairs with aCNBIGRNNA (current-price). Together the four green note issuance series provide redundant coverage of China's green bond primary market from different angles (price basis, registry source, or bond sub-type). Published monthly as part of Shanghai Clearing House green finance statistics.
rics.how_to_use: The primary use case for aCNBIGRNNP versus aCNBIGRNCP is cross-validation: if the two volume series report significantly different values, one may cover interbank and the other exchange-listed green notes. For China green bond market sizing, summing across both registries (Shanghai Clearing House + ChinaBond) and both market segments (interbank + exchange) gives the broadest measure. Analysts building ESG/green finance dashboards should use these four series alongside aCNBICCBNA for green penetration rate tracking.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Medium-term Notes
rics.meaning: Monthly gross issuance of Medium-Term Notes (MTN, 中期票据) via Shanghai Clearing House. MTNs are issued under NAFMII supervision by Chinese corporates, typically with 3-year or 5-year maturities, as the primary medium-term debt financing instrument for large and mid-sized enterprises outside the banking system. Monthly MTN issuance regularly exceeds CNY 400–800 billion, making MTNs the largest component of China's corporate credit bond market with over CNY 13 trillion outstanding.
rics.how_to_use: MTN issuance is the benchmark corporate credit primary market indicator. Use month-on-month changes to detect shifts in corporate financing demand and market conditions. A compression in MTN-over-CDB spreads drives issuance surges; spread widening chokes issuance. Pair aCNBIMTNCA with aCNBCMTNCA (outstanding stock) to compute net MTN issuance (primary minus scheduled maturities); positive net issuance indicates growing corporate bond debt. The 3Y and 5Y MTN pricing benchmarks are watched as the investable credit curve for Chinese A-rated corporate borrowers.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Non-bank financial institution bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Non-bank Financial Institution Bonds (Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly issuance of bonds by non-bank financial institutions (NBFI) registered at Shanghai Clearing House — including securities companies, consumer finance companies, trust companies, and financial leasing companies. NBFI bonds fund short-term wholesale operations and medium-term balance-sheet growth. The 'CP' suffix may denote transaction count or current-price basis. Monthly NBFI bond issuance is episodic, reflecting seasonal broker funding cycles and regulatory leverage limits.
rics.how_to_use: NBFI bond issuance is a financial-sector leverage indicator. Securities company bond and CP issuance peaks in Q1 (annual funding needs) and around market activity surges. Monitor alongside aCNBDNFBNA (NBFI outstanding stock) and aCNBCSCBCA (short-term broker financing bond depository) to build a complete NBFI wholesale funding picture. A sudden drop in NBFI bond issuance, especially if accompanied by falling settlement volumes (aCNBSNFCNA), signals broker deleveraging that may foreshadow wider market stress.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Panda bonds, Current Prices, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Panda Bonds (CNY, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly gross issuance of panda bonds (熊猫债) in CNY current-price terms, registered at Shanghai Clearing House. Panda bonds are CNY-denominated bonds issued by non-Chinese entities — including sovereign issuers from Belt and Road countries (Hungary, South Korea), multilateral development banks (World Bank, ADB, AIIB), and foreign corporations and financial institutions — in China's onshore bond market. Annual panda bond issuance has grown from CNY 20–30 billion in 2018 to CNY 150–250 billion by the mid-2020s.
rics.how_to_use: Panda bond issuance is the most direct indicator of CNY internationalisation in the primary bond market. Rising issuance signals that foreign entities find CNY funding attractive — typically when CNY interest rates are competitive versus offshore alternatives and when regulatory barriers are low. The spread between panda bond yields and comparable CGB yields reveals the 'panda premium' demanded by the onshore market for foreign-issuer credit risk. Monitor alongside aCNBIPDBNP (volume) and aCNIPPDBNA (interest paid) for the full panda bond market lifecycle.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Panda bonds, Volume, Stocks, Bonds & Funds, Monthly, Shanghai Clearing House
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Panda Bonds (volume, Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly panda bond issuance in volume/notional terms from Shanghai Clearing House, the volume counterpart to aCNBIPDBNA. The 'NP' suffix denotes notional value or possibly transaction count, providing the face-value basis for panda bond issuance analysis. Panda bonds are typically issued at or near par, so divergence between the CNY-price (aCNBIPDBNA) and notional (aCNBIPDBNP) series is modest in most periods.
rics.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNBIPDBNA to verify panda bond issuance pricing — bonds issued at discount to par will show aCNBIPDBNA < aCNBIPDBNP. A transaction-count interpretation of aCNBIPDBNP enables average deal size calculation: dividing CNY value by count gives average panda bond size, which has grown as larger foreign sovereigns and multinational corporates enter the market. Pair with aCNIPPDBNA (interest paid) to track the total financing cost flow to foreign issuers and understand CNY borrowing cost attractiveness.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Short-term Securities Companies Financing Bonds
rics.subcategory: Bond Issuance — Short-term Securities Co. Financing Bonds (Shanghai CH)
rics.meaning: Monthly gross issuance of short-term securities company financing bonds (证券公司短期融资券) registered at Shanghai Clearing House. These instruments — with maturities typically under 1 year — are the primary wholesale short-term funding tool for Chinese broker-dealers, supplementing interbank repo for proprietary trading and market-making operations. Issuance volumes are sensitive to market conditions and regulatory leverage caps on securities firms.
rics.how_to_use: Securities company short-term bond issuance is a high-frequency broker leverage indicator. Peaks in aCNBISCBNA typically coincide with bull equity markets (brokers funding expanded proprietary positions) or bond market rallies (funding leveraged bond carry trades). Compare with aCNBCSCBCA (outstanding depository stock) to compute net issuance. Abrupt declines in issuance — especially if short-term rather than reflecting seasonal patterns — can precede broker balance-sheet stress. Pair with aCNBINFICP and aCNBSNFCNA for a complete NBFI funding cycle analysis.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Standardized Notes
rics.meaning: Monthly gross issuance of standardized notes (标准化票据, or 'Biao Piao') from Shanghai Clearing House. Standardized notes are a relatively new PBOC-initiated instrument (pilot launched 2020) that converts non-standard credit assets (bank acceptance drafts, commercial bills) into tradeable standardized notes through a trust or SPV structure. This instrument aims to bridge bank lending and the capital market, improving credit asset liquidity and market transparency.
rics.how_to_use: Standardized notes represent a policy experiment in formalising China's commercial paper and supply-chain finance markets. Rising issuance signals successful market uptake of this PBOC initiative; the standardized note market, if it scales, would improve SME access to capital market funding and reduce reliance on bank acceptance drafts. Compare issuance pace against target levels set by PBOC pilots to assess policy execution. From a structural perspective, standardized note growth would eventually reduce commercial paper volumes (aCNBCCMPCA) as the market migrates to the more transparent format.

rics.description: Bonds Issuance: Total
rics.meaning: Monthly total bond issuance across all categories registered at Shanghai Clearing House — the sum of ABS, corporate credit bonds (MTN, CP, SCP, SME notes), green notes, panda bonds, financial bonds, NBFI bonds, standardized notes, and securities company short-term financing bonds. Shanghai Clearing House is the central registry for NAFMII-supervised instruments; its issuance total complements the ChinaBond issuance total (aCNOVBISNA) for a combined picture of the whole onshore bond primary market.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the headline Shanghai Clearing House primary market gauge. Combined with ChinaBond-registered issuance (aCNOVBISNA), this gives the closest estimate of total Chinese bond market gross issuance. Month-on-month fluctuations reflect corporate funding cycle seasonality (Q1 low, Q2-Q4 higher), policy windows, and rate environment. Compare the Shanghai CH total with aCNBRTOTNA (total redemptions, both registries) to estimate net issuance, the key metric for bond market supply pressure on interest rates.

rics.description: Bonds Redemption: Total
rics.meaning: Monthly total principal redemptions (到期兑付) across all bond categories — covering both ChinaBond-registered (CGBs, LGBs, policy bank bonds, commercial bank bonds) and Shanghai Clearing House-registered instruments (MTNs, CP, ABS). This represents scheduled principal repayments as bonds mature, providing the 'supply reduction' counterpart to gross issuance. China's bond market has substantial rolling maturities given the large stock of outstanding bonds — monthly redemptions regularly exceed CNY 3–6 trillion.
rics.how_to_use: Net issuance = gross issuance (aCNOVBISNA or aCNBITOTNP) minus redemptions (aCNBRTOTNA). Net issuance is the true addition to bond market debt and the net supply pressure on yields. In months with very high redemptions, even substantial gross issuance may result in near-zero net issuance — providing a temporary relief valve for yield pressure. Track rolling 12-month cumulative net issuance vs GDP for debt-to-GDP dynamics. Analyse the redemption schedule by category to anticipate monthly supply-demand imbalances.

rics.description: Commercial Papers - Credit Cooperatives
rics.subcategory: Commercial Paper Holding Structure — Credit Cooperatives
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on commercial paper (CP and SCP) held by credit cooperatives. Credit cooperatives are small deposit-taking institutions that invest in CP primarily for short-duration yield management — placing surplus liquidity in 3-to-9-month corporate paper rather than in lower-yielding interbank deposits. Their CP holdings are modest but reflect small-institution access to the corporate short-term debt market.
rics.how_to_use: Credit cooperative CP holdings are a tail-risk indicator for CP market demand breadth. When smaller institutions pull back from CP investment (falling aCNHCCPCCA), it often signals credit concerns about specific issuers or general risk aversion at the smaller-institution tier — particularly relevant if deterioration follows a corporate CP default. Compare with aCNHCCPDFA (depository financial institution aggregate CP holdings) to assess whether small institutions are tracking or diverging from the larger bank trend in CP investment appetite.

rics.description: Commercial Papers - Depository Financial Institutions
rics.subcategory: Commercial Paper Holding Structure — Depository Financial Institutions
rics.meaning: Monthly Shanghai Clearing House data on commercial paper (CP and SCP) held by all depository financial institutions — commercial banks, policy banks, credit cooperatives, and postal savings institutions. Banks are the largest CP investors, treating corporate CP as a short-duration asset for liquidity management. Depository institution CP demand is the anchor of the corporate short-term bond market, absorbing a large share of each new issuance. Published monthly as part of Shanghai Clearing House's CP investor statistics.
rics.how_to_use: Depository institution CP holdings are the primary demand indicator for China's corporate short-term bond market. Compare month-on-month changes with aCNBCCMPCA (total CP outstanding) to derive the depository institution share. When banks dominate CP holdings, CP yields trade close to policy rates; when non-bank institutions grow their share, CP yields may be more sensitive to credit differentiation. A sharp drop in bank CP holdings alongside rising CP yields signals tightening bank liquidity or credit-quality concerns about specific corporate CP issuers.
